jobs.description:
Board Advisor (Volunteer)

Mothers to Daughters

About Mothers to Daughters:

Mothers to Daughters (M2D) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit dedicated to empowering women across generations through leadership and entrepreneurship training, educational workshops, and networking opportunities. Through intergenerational mentorship and community service, M2D advances gender equality, fosters leadership, and equips women to drive social and economic change in their communities. This handbook outlines our values, policies, and operational procedures to guide team members in fulfilling our mission.

Our Mission at Mothers to Daughters is to accelerate the personal and professional growth of women by connecting them with the lived experiences, authentic insights, and transformative wisdom of successful women. Through intergenerational mentorship, we foster a legacy of economic empowerment, social resilience, and impact-driven innovation, equipping women to lead, innovate, and build sustainable solutions that transcend generations.

Our Vision is a world where women of all generations thrive through the power of intergenerational wisdom, driving inclusivity and gender equity for lasting global impact. By bridging generations, amplifying voices, and breaking down barriers, we aim to create a future where women are elevated to the heights they deserve—leading, innovating, and shaping a more equitable and prosperous world for all.

Our Core Values at Mothers to Daughters are:

  • UnwaveringRespect

    • We honor diverse perspectives and experiences, fostering an environment where every voice is valued.

    • We believe in mutual respect between generations, recognizing the wisdom of experience and the disruptive innovation of youth.

    • We encourage bold yet respectful dialogue in discussions around gender equality, relationships, and personal development.

  • Purpose driven-Trust

    • We prioritize transparency, accountability, and credibility, ensuring that our members, mentors, and sponsors feel confident in our work.

    • We believe trust is the cornerstone of meaningful mentorship, enabling honest, courageous conversations and impactful guidance.

    • We commit to upholding the integrity of our mission, maintaining the highest ethical standards in all our partnerships and programs.

  • Synergistic Collaboration

    • We recognize that transformative change happens when we work together across generations, cultures, and industries.

    • We actively forge alliances with organizations that align with our mission, including men’s groups working toward gender equity.

    • We foster a culture of dynamic knowledge-sharing, ensuring that mentorship is a two-way exchange where both mentors and mentees grow together.

  • Transformational Empathy

    • We understand that each woman’s journey is unique, committing to creating a safe space for shared experiences and personal growth.

    • We recognize societal and personal challenges women face and approach solutions with compassion and pragmatic action.

    • We champion vulnerability as a strength, encouraging open discussions about both breakthroughs and setbacks.

  • Impact-Driven Entrepreneurial Spirit

    • We believe in equipping women with the skills, mindset, and resources to take ownership of their futures—whether through career advancement, leadership, or business ventures.

    • We encourage innovation, agility, and adaptability, ensuring our programs evolve to meet the shifting needs of our global community.

    • We emphasize bold resilience, helping women break barriers, embrace risk, and lead with confidence.

  • Unapologetic Authenticity

    • We embrace and celebrate individuality, encouraging women to bring their whole selves to the table.

    • We champion unapologetic self-expression, ensuring that every woman’s voice is heard, respected, and amplified.

    • We commit to honest, transparent communication, rejecting performative feminism in favor of practical, high-impact actions that drive real change.

  • Future-focused Innovation

    • We embrace bold, transformative thinking, pushing boundaries to create solutions that redefine possibilities for women.

    • We leverage technology, data, and creativity to amplify mentorship, leadership, and economic empowerment initiatives.

    • We foster a culture of continuous learning and reinvention, ensuring that women stay ahead in an ever-evolving global landscape.

Position Overview:

We are seeking a Board Advisor with board governance expertise. The successful candidate will have deep understanding of international development issues, strong analytical skills, proven experience in designing and implementing social impact programs, excellent communication abilities, and a network within the UN system and broader social impact. As part of our dynamic and mission-driven team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of our organization and advancing our mission.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Offer high-level strategic advice that usually focuses on long-term business growth, innovation, and risk management.

  • Prove up-to-date insights into trends, regulatory changes, and advancements in the social impact space.

  • Connect the organization with potential business partners, investors, and clients, thereby opening new opportunities.

  • Providing mentorship to executives on topics such as leadership, development, crisis management, or succession planning.

  • Give insights into governance best practices to help companies stay aligned with their goals and values.

Qualifications and Skills:

  • UN experience:

    • Prior work with UN agencies, programs, or funds in a relevant capacity (e.g., policy development, program management, advocacy)

    • Familiarity with UN frameworks, procedures, and decision-making processes

    • Understanding of the UN system's strengths and limitations

  • Social impact expertise:

    • Proven track record in designing and implementing social impact initiatives across diverse areas like poverty alleviation, education, health, climate change adaptation, or gender equality

    • Expertise in developing and measuring social impact metrics

    • Knowledge of best practices in social impact assessment and reporting

  • Strategic thinking:

    • Capacity to develop comprehensive strategic plans aligned with UN goals and organizational priorities

    • Ability to identify emerging trends and potential opportunities in the social impact landscape

    • Skillful at navigating complex political and stakeholder dynamics

  • Communication and advocacy skills:

    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills to effectively present complex issues to diverse audiences

    • Proven ability to advocate for social impact initiatives at various levels, including with policymakers and donors

    • Expertise in building strong relationships with key stakeholders

  • Leadership and collaboration:

    • Ability to lead and facilitate collaborative efforts with diverse teams and stakeholders

    • Strong interpersonal skills to build consensus and foster positive working relationships

Commitment:

  • Serve at the organization for 1 year.

  • Ability to meet and collaborate weekly via Zoom, Google Drive, Microsoft and Slack with the team.

  • Ability to attend monthly Board Meetings and Team All Hands via Zoom.

  • Approximate time commitment: 2 hours monthly

Benefits:

  • The opportunity to make a meaningful impact in empowering the next generation of women leaders.

  • Enhance the impact of our programs on women's economic advancement, intellectual growth, and social mobility.

  • Access to our network of elite professionals (business executives, entrepreneurs, community leaders etc) and professional development opportunities through board service.

How to Apply:

Interested candidates should fill out the application form and submit their resume and cover letter.

Mothers to Daughters is an equal opportunity organization and encourages applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.description:
Tailored Brands, Inc. is a leading omni-channel specialty retailer of menswear, including suits and a broad selection of business casual offerings as well as the largest provider of tuxedo rental products in the U.S. and Canada. We operate retail stores in all 50 states and Canada. Our U.S. retail stores are operated under the brand names of Men’s Wearhouse, Jos. A. Bank, Men’s Wearhouse and Tux, and K&G Fashion.Our Canadian stores are operated under the brand name of Moores in ten provinces. Our purpose is to help our customers love how they look for moments that matter. We accomplish this by providing a personal, convenient, one-of-a-kind shopping experience with compelling products and world-class service. We help fulfill this mission by providing our employees with an engaging and inclusive workplace focused on teamwork, growth and respect. If you want to make a difference, be part of a great team and grow, you might be a perfect fit.

About the Job

We currently have an exciting opportunity for a Sr. Director, Real Estate to join our Real Estate team. Reporting to the SVP of Real Estate and Construction, this executive leader will have enterprise accountability for the strategy, governance and execution of Tailored Brands’ real estate program across all brands and markets. The Sr. Director will lead, coach and develop the Directors responsible for market strategy, site selection, lease negotiations, portfolio optimization and corporate real estate, ensuring consistent standards, disciplined execution and strong financial outcomes. This position will oversee the transactional management and strategic planning for retail stores, corporate offices, HUBs, Distribution Centers and other leased or owned properties. The role will provide senior leadership for relocation, replacement, renewal, expansion, closure, disposition and other real estate initiatives, serving as a key advisor to the SVP of Real Estate and Construction and executive partners across the Company.

What You’ll Do | Key Accountabilities

  • Leads and develops the Directors across the Real Estate organization by establishing clear accountability, priorities, performance expectations and operating rhythms; builds bench strength through coaching, mentoring, succession planning and effective talent management.
  • Establishes portfolio governance, decision criteria, approval processes and key performance indicators to ensure consistent, data-driven recommendations and execution across all real estate functions.
  • Partners with executive and cross-functional teams to identify opportunities, align real estate actions with corporate and brand strategies, and translate business priorities into actionable market and portfolio plans.
  • Oversees analysis of demographics, income levels, customer density, competitive activity, traffic patterns, retail synergies and other market data to determine site feasibility, portfolio opportunities and investment priorities.
  • Directs the development and performance management of the broker and developer network. Establishes company standards for site development and economic terms, ensures the Directors and brokers apply those standards consistently, and monitors results and service quality.
  • Provides senior oversight of lease and transaction negotiations, including rent and lease terms, site conditions, landlord contributions, business points and legal requirements. Serves as an escalation point for complex, high-value or strategically important negotiations in partnership with Real Estate and Legal leaders.
  • Maintains senior relationships with landlords, developers, brokers and strategic partners; represents Tailored Brands in important portfolio discussions and ensures the Company is positioned for future development opportunities.
  • Establishes disciplined pipeline, project management and reporting practices across the organization, ensuring timely escalation of risks, decisions, dependencies and resource needs.
  • Owns the accuracy and credibility of the new-store and real estate initiative pipeline, including 12- to 24-month opening projections, portfolio actions, lease events and other enterprise commitments.
  • Provides executive oversight of reporting for existing-location lease actions, new-store activity, owned assets, corporate properties and other real estate initiatives; uses reporting to drive accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Champions an owner’s mindset, balancing customer and brand needs with long-term portfolio value, risk management, capital discipline and total occupancy economics.
  • Oversees all transactions involving the owned-assets portfolio, including acquisitions, dispositions and sale-leaseback transactions, in coordination with Finance, Legal and other stakeholders.
  • Has strategic oversight of the portfolio of logistics and transportation HUBs, Distribution Centers, Corporate Offices and other corporate-supporting locations, including portfolio planning, lease strategy, capital needs and business continuity considerations.
  • Serves as a senior advisor to the SVP of Real Estate and Construction and executive leadership on enterprise real estate matters and leads other strategic initiatives as assigned.

Skills & Experience

  • Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s degree required in Business, Real Estate or a related field; 15+ years of relevant experience, including significant experience leading real estate teams and complex, multi-market programs.
  • Preferred Requirements: Master’s degree in Business, Real Estate or a related field; 7+ years of people-leadership experience and a demonstrated track record overseeing retail real estate site selection, lease negotiations, portfolio strategy and high-volume transaction execution (20+ annual new deals at the team level).
  • Executive-level verbal and written communication skills; highly organized, detail-oriented and proficient in Microsoft Office and presentation tools.
  • Strong financial acumen, including the ability to interpret P&L statements, evaluate investment returns and occupancy economics, and guide the development of effective action plans tied to strategic objectives.
  • Knowledge of demographic mapping, market planning and real estate analytics tools required.
  • Exceptional people-leadership skills with the ability to attract, develop, coach and retain high-performing Directors and broader real estate teams.
  • Strong negotiation, influence and executive presence, with the ability to build alignment and make sound decisions at all levels of the organization and with external partners.
  • Deep understanding of complex leases, transaction structures, corresponding legal terms and real estate risk management.
  • Proficient in financial analysis, spreadsheets, presentations, portfolio reporting, pipeline management and enterprise program management.
  • Strategic thinker who can manage multiple priorities, make decisions with incomplete information, create operating discipline and drive accountability across a distributed organization.
Please note that you do not need to qualify for all requirements to be considered. We encourage you to apply if you can meet most of the requirements and are comfortable opening a dialog to be considered.

Work Environment, Physical & Mental Demands

  • Ability to sit and work at a computer keyboard for extended periods of time
  • Ability to stoop, kneel, bend at the waist, and reach daily
  • Able to lift and move up to 25 pounds occasionally
  • Must utilize visual acuity, speech and hearing, hand and eye coordination and manual dexterity necessary to operate a computer and office equipment
  • Hours regularly 40 hours per week, as work dictates, from remote location
  • Must be based on the East Coast or West Coast, near a major metropolitan airport.
  • A minimum of 25% travel is required, including market trips, industry conventions and other events, landlord and developer portfolio meetings, team meetings and other travel as designated by the SVP of Real Estate and Construction.

Benefits

This role is eligible for health, dental and vision insurance, prescription drug, retirement savings (401k, employer-funded retirement plans, deferred compensation, and other defined-benefit or defined-contribution), life insurance, accident and disability, paid time off for sick leave, vacation, bereavement, jury duty, holidays (9 days per year), wellbeing program, commuter, adoption assistance, legal services, and employee merchandise discounts.

Work-Life Balance

We understand the demands of work, school, family, and personal responsibilities. Through our work-life resources and programs we offer services for every stage of life to help you manage the day-to-day needs. We offer programs such as:
  • Meeting-Free Fridays (encouraged) | so you can catch up on work and self-development
  • Summer Fridays | from Memorial Day to Labor Day so you can enjoy a head-start to the weekend
  • Holiday Early Departure | close out early the business day before a company observed holiday
The starting salary for this position is $186,596-$248,747. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on factors such as skills, experience, and qualifications. Other compensation may include a 25% Annual Incentive Plan (AIP) bonus paid out according to policy. Base pay information is based on market location and may be subject to prevailing wage laws, if applicable.
Note: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities or qualifications associated with this job.

jobs.description:
Distinguished is a leading national insurance Program Manager providing specialized insurance programs to brokers and agents with specific expertise in Real Estate, Community Associations, Hospitality, Fine Art/Collectibles, Restaurants, Surety, Transactional Risk and Environmental/Construction Professional. Distinguished partners with a select group of highly rated insurance companies to provide exclusive programs to our national network of 4,000 agencies and brokerages. You will have an opportunity to work with an energetic, passionate team that is committed to growth by helping our customers grow their business and building a best-in-class system, as well as a great place to work.

You will be a New BusinessUnderwriter that is part of our Community Associations program which specializes and serves a variety of associations such as condominiums, homeowners, and cooperatives for new business and renewals. The primary responsibilities include account pipeline management, risk selection, qualification, and pricing within the program guidelines and objectives, and selling the proposal to insurance brokers. This involves communicating, working, and negotiating directly with brokers and includes duties such as ensuring the accuracy of underwriting information, determining eligibility, ensuring insurance files are well documented, responding to questions and addressing issues, and servicing change requests.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Solicit and shepherd new submissions based on program appetite.
  • Build and manage a new business pipeline through outbound interaction with brokers including outbound phone calls and in-person broker visits.
  • Gather competitor information and market intelligence and understand trends to identify opportunities for improvements to products and pricing.
  • Manage new submissions to ensure proper risk selection, premium and coverage.
  • Underwrite community association risks by identifying and analyzing risk exposures, loss frequency and severity against desired coverage.
  • Provide and create solutions for a broad range of inquiries from brokers and team members.
  • Seek out cross marketing opportunities.
  • Manage renewals to maximize policy retention including midterm servicing with various carriers and brokers, within your authority in an assigned territory.
  • Develop relationships with brokers, with the "customer experience" in mind, and deliver exceptional experiences with every interaction, in all modes of communication.
  • Work independently within deadlines while understanding the necessity for appropriate prioritization, communicating and coordinating work efforts with stakeholders.
  • Maintain quality control, compliance and proper documentation.
  • Promote teamwork and organizational success, while accepting accountability and ownership, celebrating successes and learning from past mistakes.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency through process, procedure, and system improvements.
  • Participate in other company projects and new initiatives.

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education/experience.
  • Minimum 8 years of in-depth commercial package policy underwriting experience.
  • Community Associations with high CAT exposure experience preferred.
  • Having a professional designation(s) is a plus.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including negotiation skills with the ability to influence and persuade.
  • Analytical and quantitative skills.
  • Must be self-driven, detail-oriented, flexible/adaptable, comfortable in a growing ever-changing organization, and have strong organizational skills including time-management and prioritization.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of commercial lines products.
  • Must possess strong and effective negotiation, analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to effectively and independently manage complex workload while exhibiting very sound judgment.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain broker relationships.
  • Exemplify superior teamwork
  • Must possess the ability to effectively penetrate and increase our new business writings.
  • Strong leadership, communication, influencing, presentation, negotiation, planning and team effectiveness skills.
  • Some limited travel may be required.

LOCATION
This is a remote position.

COMPENSATION & PERKS
  • $100,000 - $120,000 base salary plus bonus. Salary commensurate with knowledge, skills, experience, and geographic location.
  • Summer Fridays (Leave at 2:00PM all Fridays from Memorial Day to Labor Day).
  • Full healthcare coverage including Medical, Vision, and Dental.
  • 401k - 4% company match. Immediately 100% vested.

jobs.description:
DevOps Staff Platform Engineer

Location: Remote (Canada)

Compensation: $135,000 - $170,000 CAD + bonus + meaningful equity

About Orion Digital

Orion Digital Corp (NASDAQ/TSX: ORIO) is a publicly listed Canadian fintech operating a multi-engine financial platform spanning lending (Mogo), payments (Carta), and wealth (Intelligent Investing).

We have moved past the traditional fintech model. Capital allocation, decisioning, and risk management sit at the core of how the business creates value, and AI runs as an enabling layer across the platform rather than as a standalone product narrative. That layer is real and in use, and the work now is making it faster, safer, and harder to break.

Why this role exists

This role builds that layer.

Platform engineering here is not a support function. Multiple business lines, regulated entities, and a public company's reporting obligations all run on infrastructure this team owns. Every deployment path, permission boundary, and audit trail either makes faster decisioning possible or quietly caps how fast the business can move.

Which means the platform is where the strategy succeeds or stalls. If deploying takes a day, if an agent cannot safely touch production, if nobody can tell what changed and why, the enabling layer stays theoretical. We are hiring a Staff Platform Engineer to build it properly.

The shift we are hiring for

Most platform teams build for human developers. Ours builds for humans and agents, across multiple business lines and regulated entities. That changes the job:

  • Golden paths become machine-executable contracts, not wiki pages. An agent has to be able to discover them, invoke them, and verify the result.
  • Every probabilistic step needs a deterministic gate behind it. Tests, policy checks, and schema validation stop being hygiene and become the control system that lets autonomy scale safely.
  • Agents are identities. They need scoped credentials, bounded blast radius, and audit trails that hold up across lending, payments, and securities regulation.
  • Observability has to answer a new question. Not just "is the service healthy" but "did the agent do the right thing, and how do we know."

If that is already how you think about the problem, keep reading.

What you will do

Build the substrate for agentic engineering

  • Design and run the execution environments agents work in: sandboxed, reproducible, permissioned, disposable.
  • Stand up and own our MCP and tool-gateway layer so agents reach infrastructure through governed interfaces instead of ad hoc credentials.
  • Turn CI/CD into a validation loop: fast deterministic gates an agent can retry against until it passes, with humans on the loop rather than in it.

Own the platform

  • Multi-cloud Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and GitOps (ArgoCD) delivery. Hands on keyboard, not diagrams.
  • Drive infrastructure modernization across our cloud environments, including the unglamorous parts: dependency mapping, and documentation that survives your absence.
  • Serve every product line without building a separate platform for each one. Where they genuinely differ, respect it. Where they have drifted for no reason, converge them.
  • Treat security and compliance as design constraints from the first commit rather than a review at the end.

Take toil off the company

  • Push autonomous remediation into the paths that page people today. The target is alerts that resolve themselves and incidents where the first responder is an agent arriving with a hypothesis already tested.
  • Own the numbers: deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, and the share of operational work running without a human in the middle. Move them quarter over quarter.
  • Work outside engineering too. Operations, compliance, and support are full of repetitive work a well-built platform can absorb.

What you need

Non-negotiable

  • Deep, current production experience with Kubernetes, Terraform, and a modern GitOps deployment stack. You have owned what you built, including running it in production rather than handing it off once it shipped.
  • Real cloud depth. We run across AWS and OCI, so experience in both is an advantage, but what matters is genuine production depth in at least one and the appetite to get fluent in the other quickly.
  • You run coding and ops agents as part of your daily work, and you can show us. Sustained real use on real systems (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent, plus whatever you have wired together yourself), not a trial and an opinion. Be ready to walk through something you shipped this month where an agent did most of the typing and you did the judging.
  • Strong opinions about where autonomy belongs and where it does not, informed by having been burned at least once.
  • Writing clear enough to be read by a junior engineer and a model.

Advantage

  • You have built internal developer platforms, MCP servers, or agent tooling that other engineers actually adopted.
  • Non-human identity, secrets architecture, or policy-as-code in a regulated environment.
  • Re-platforming at scale, especially where the old system could not go down.
  • Opinions about how to evaluate infrastructure agents. Almost nobody has these yet.

We are not screening on years of experience as a proxy for capability. We will look at what you have built and how fast you build.

How we work

  • Small teams, high ownership, short distance between decision and deployment.
  • We would rather collaborate than dictate, and we know when to do it well versus when to do it quickly.
  • Output is the measure.

This is an operations-first role, not a highly technical data engineering position. You’ll coordinate freight and inventory, maintain accurate operational data, manage Shopify information, build reports and dashboards, and use spreadsheets to help the business make better operational decisions.

You’ll also use modern AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude to streamline repetitive work, improve reporting, and make internal processes more efficient.

  • Develop practical AI-assisted processes that improve speed and accuracy.

  • Continuously identify opportunities to make operations more efficient.

  • You’re highly organized and comfortable managing multiple operational workflows.
  • You understand how logistics, inventory, and e-commerce operations connect.
  • You enjoy working with spreadsheets and turning operational data into useful insights.
  • You proactively identify problems rather than waiting for them to escalate.

  • Experience creating automated reports or dashboards.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted data analysis and workflow automation.
  • Experience collaborating with developers on operational integrations.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

You may:

  • Review inventory levels and upcoming stock requirements.
  • Track active freight shipments and follow up with warehouse partners.
  • Create or update purchase orders.
  • Update Shopify and operational records.
  • Maintain inventory and logistics spreadsheets.

Key Metrics for Success

What Happens After You Apply

jobs.description:
Pediatrics Admin & Front Office Support

Remote | Pediatrics | Part-Time, 30 hours/week initially | $5-$6/hour
Target Start Date: September 14, 2026
Future Schedule: Expected to increase to approximately 40 hours/week as the practice opens and patient volume grows

About the Role

We are looking for a highly organized, proactive, and adaptable Virtual Medical Assistant to support a growing pediatric practice during its pre-opening and early growth stages.

This is not a traditional, narrowly defined Medical VA position. During the startup phase, you will work closely with the physician as an administrative and personal assistant, helping coordinate meetings, calendars, vendors, projects, communications, and clinic setup activities.

As the practice begins seeing patients, your responsibilities will gradually transition toward front-office and medical administrative support, including scheduling, patient intake, insurance verification, and patient communication.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a growing environment where priorities can change, takes ownership without needing constant reminders, and can independently identify what needs to be done next.

Key Responsibilities

1. Executive, Administrative & Calendar Support

  • Manage and organize the physician's calendars, ensuring meetings, deadlines, agendas, links, documents, and preparation materials are consolidated in one place.

  • Attend administrative and vendor meetings as needed, take clear notes, document action items, and help ensure important follow-ups are completed.

  • Serve as a proactive accountability partner by tracking deadlines, projects, tasks, and outstanding items without requiring constant reminders.

2. Front Office & Patient Communication

  • Manage incoming patient calls, emails, texts, voicemails, and initial inquiries professionally once the clinic begins accepting patients.

  • Assist prospective and existing families with scheduling, follow-ups, basic questions, and other front-office communication needs.

  • Provide a warm, professional first point of contact that reflects the patient-centered experience expected from a pediatric practice.

3. Patient Scheduling, Intake & Registration

  • Coordinate end-to-end patient scheduling, including new patient appointments, follow-ups, rescheduling, and appointment-related communication.

  • Support patient intake and check-in by ensuring required demographic, administrative, and insurance information is collected accurately.

  • Maintain organized patient information and appointment records within eClinicalWorks (eCW) while following established clinic workflows.

4. Insurance Verification & Administrative Support

  • Verify commercial insurance coverage and determine whether patient insurance plans are active, pending, or require additional follow-up.

  • Complete insurance eligibility and benefit verification before appointments and document findings accurately for the practice.

  • Assist with insurance-related administrative tasks and potentially prior authorizations as clinic processes expand.

5. Vendor, Research & Project Coordination

  • Research vendors, clinic equipment, software, and other operational needs and compare available options based on cost, features, and suitability.

  • Organize research findings, pricing comparisons, project updates, and recommendations using spreadsheets and other tracking tools.

  • Follow up with vendors and internal stakeholders to keep clinic setup projects progressing according to established timelines.

6. Process Documentation & SOP Development

  • Document recurring workflows and administrative processes as the clinic develops its operating procedures.

  • Create clear step-by-step SOPs for tasks such as scheduling, patient communication, insurance verification, and other recurring activities.

  • Continuously identify opportunities to organize, standardize, and improve workflows as the practice grows.

Must-Have Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with eClinicalWorks (eCW) is REQUIRED. Candidates without prior eCW experience should not be considered.

  • 1+ years previous experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant, Medical Assistant, Healthcare Administrative Assistant, or similar healthcare support professional.

  • Strong administrative, organizational, calendar-management, and task-management skills.

  • Excellent written and spoken English with the confidence to communicate professionally with patients, families, vendors, and healthcare professionals.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills and the ability to organize information, research, projects, and workflows independently.

  • Highly proactive and able to recognize what needs attention without waiting to be reminded.

  • Comfortable working in a startup-style environment where responsibilities and priorities may evolve.

  • Able to multitask effectively while maintaining strong attention to detail.

  • Comfortable using required secure networks, clinic systems, and productivity tracking software.

Strongly Preferred

  • Previous experience working in pediatrics.

  • Experience performing commercial insurance verification.

  • Experience handling prior authorizations for commercial insurance or HMO plans.

  • Experience supporting a physician, clinic owner, executive, or small medical practice.

  • Basic Canva or graphic-editing skills for simple social media or clinic content.

Tools & Systems

Candidates may work with:

  • eClinicalWorks (eCW) EMR, REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

  • RingRX or similar HIPAA-compliant phone systems

  • Google Calendar or other multi-calendar systems

  • Google Sheets or similar spreadsheet tools

  • Canva

  • Secure private networks/VPNs

  • Productivity tracking software

What Success Looks Like

You will succeed in this role if you become someone the physician can trust to take ownership of responsibilities, anticipate what needs to happen next, and keep important tasks from falling through the cracks.

You should be able to work independently, organize competing priorities, communicate professionally with families, and help create systems that allow the physician to focus more heavily on patient care.

As the practice grows, success will also mean helping create a smooth patient experience from the first phone call through scheduling, intake, insurance verification, and ongoing follow-up.

jobs.excerpt: Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.
jobs.description:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease.

Job overview:

We are hiring a Engineering Manager to lead two squads building Omada’s Platform and Engineering Systems. These squads own problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what they ship. You are responsible for those squads: what they work on, in what order, and how your people and teams grow.

As a Engineering Manager, you ship code alongside your AI-powered engineers. You own the execution and will run the squad’s rituals: iteration shaping, prioritization, backlog refinement, and initiative estimation are your calls. Being in charge means you have an opinion about the tradeoffs you and the squad are making, and are comfortable partnering with the squad’s stakeholders and finding solutions to problems, should they arise.

You partner closely with stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Design, IT, InfoSec, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and beyond. Your relationships with the people in those departments will be very important. You will manage millions of dollars in annual vendor budget and spending, through key contracts including Amazon Web Services, Datadog, Gitlab, and Anthropic. You will be responsible for annual internal and external audit controls, and must help your teams develop automation and evidence management processes to streamline audit responses.

About you:

You are comfortable being accountable for what your squad ships. You still write code, and you want to. This role ships production work every sprint, off the critical path, in the same codebase and the same agentic workflows as your squad: you’ll feel the friction your people feel because you experience it first-hand.

You are an experienced engineering leader, and you are opinionated about the systems you maintain. You understand why the most important work must be done, and you own the roadmap that will get it done. You are respected technically, but do not need to be the strongest engineer in the squad: your work generally stays off the critical path, but you must possess the fundamental understanding to know what great looks like, and the communication skills to build strong relationships with your teams and colleagues.

You are opinionated about where AI-assisted development helps and where it produces work someone else has to redo, because you have first-hand experience from doing the work rather than from reading about it.

Above all, you are enthusiastic about providing the best possible care for our members, and building the best engineering team of your career.

What you'll be doing:

  • Managing, Hiring, and Mentoring. You will lead 5 people. You will quickly find opportunities to expand your teams, and must have a strong perspective on how to hire amazing people. Meanwhile, you must ensure that the people who work on your teams today continue growing and challenging themselves.
  • Own the squad's delivery. Sprint shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation are yours. Make the calls, write them down, and be accountable for them.
  • Own cycle time at constant or better quality. Your squad's contribution to it is yours to move and yours to explain.
  • Ship code. Production work every sprint, off the critical path, using the same agent workflows your squad uses. This is what keeps the standing to review their work and the credibility to defend the model.
  • Grow your engineers. Omadans care about each other: we believe everyone can grow, and you will provide your reports with the best leadership they have ever experienced.
  • Own the operational health of your squad. On-call rotations, MTTR and post-incident analysis are shared work you lead.
  • Escalate early, often, and precisely. You bring tradeoffs, you use your engineering and product taste to come up with recommendations.
  • You will hire the new generation of AI-augmented Omadans. We believe in co-intelligence: we will continue hiring amazing humans, and help them build a career with us.

What you need for this role:

  • 8+ years in software engineering, including at least 2 years managing engineers, or equivalent experience leading delivery for a team you were accountable for.
  • A track record shipping mission-critical software to production, and living with it afterwards: we all make mistakes, what separates you from others is that you own these, and use this as an opportunity to build something even greater.
  • The ability to build a roadmap, plan for capacity, evaluate trade-offs, and know how to negotiate with your stakeholders.
  • Experience owning prioritization and estimation for a team, including saying no, not now, and explaining why.
  • Experience giving direct developmental feedback, and at least one case where you managed someone through underperformance with real support attached.
  • Currently shipping, or recently shipping production code in at least one layer of our stack (Multi-account AWS, self-managed continuous integration, k8s, backend (Ruby, Python, ...), GitOps release management, internal tools and services) with enough range to follow the conversation in the others and review architecture decisions critically.
  • Hands-on experience directing AI agents through real world production changes, and a considered view on where they help and where they produce work someone else has to redo.
  • Understanding of CI/CD, logging, monitoring, and telemetry, at the level where you can tell whether your squad's operational story checks out or falls short.
  • A Security-mentality in everything you design and build
  • Excellent written communication. Much of this job is writing things down clearly once so they do not have to be discussed four times.

Technologies we use:

Architecture & Infrastructure: AWS (EKS, IAM, RDS, SQS, etc), Docker, GitLab, Argo/Kargo, Vault, Datadog, PagerDuty.

Application Engineering: Ruby on Rails, Python (Flask, FastAPI), React, native iOS (Swift, SwiftUI), native Android (Kotlin), PostgreSQL, GraphQL, Claude

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary with generous annual cash bonus
  • Equity grants
  • Employee stock purchasing plan (ESPP)
  • Remote first work from home culture
  • Flexible Time Off to help you rest, recharge, and connect with loved ones
  • Generous parental leave
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance (and above market employer contributions)
  • 401k retirement savings plan
  • Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA)
  • Mental Health Support Solutions
  • ...and more!

It takes a village to change health care. As we build together toward our mission, we strive to embody the following values in our day-to-day work. We hope these hold meaning for you as well as you consider Omada!

  • Cultivate Trust. We listen closely and we operate with kindness. We provide respectful and candid feedback to each other.
  • Seek Context. We ask to understand and we build connections. We do our research up front to move faster down the road.
  • Act Boldly. We innovate daily to solve problems, improve processes, and find new opportunities for our members and customers.
  • Deliver Results. We reward impact above output. We set a high bar, we’re not afraid to fail, and we take pride in our work.
  • Succeed Together. We prioritize Omada’s progress above team or individual. We have fun as we get stuff done, and we celebrate together.
  • Remember Why We’re Here. We push through the challenges of changing health care because we know the destination is worth it.

About Omada Health: Omada Health (Nasdaq: OMDA) is reverse engineering the way healthcare is delivered in America, putting the space between doctor visits–where health is won or lost–at the center of care. Today's healthcare system poorly serves chronic conditions that require ongoing support outside of the exam room, like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, and musculoskeletal conditions. Omada’s virtual-first model combines human-led care teams, connected devices, and AI-enabled technology to deliver personalized care at scale, including support for GLP-1 therapy. Omada has served more than two million members since launch across 2,000+ employers, health plans, pharmacy benefit managers, and health systems. Learn more at omadahealth.com.

jobs.excerpt: Director of Product Management, Agentic Platform Enablement Experience (APEX) Remote - US Overview: Pax8 is the global AI and cloud Marketplace for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs).
jobs.description:
Director of Product Management, Agentic Platform Enablement Experience (APEX)

Remote - US

Overview:

Pax8 is the global AI and cloud Marketplace for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). Pax8 connects service providers and technology companies on a unified platform to discover, buy, sell, deploy and manage technology solutions for SMBs. More than 47,000 IT partners and 800,000 SMBs rely on Pax8 for expertise, automation and real-time insights to stay productive, protected and prepared for the AI economy. Learn more at pax8.com.

Position Summary:

Join Pax8 as Director of Product Management for Agentic Platform Enablement Experience (APEX), the most technical product leader on the APEX team and the day-to-day owner of our agentic platform surfaces, including agent SDKs, tool use and orchestration, the internal developer platform and the autonomy and trust experience that makes agentic capability safe to adopt. You’ll be working with leadership and teams to build and deliver a product with capabilities that has no established precedent. Reporting to the VP of Product Management for APEX, you are the second seat in the practice and the one closest to the code.

This is a principal-caliber individual contributor role with people leadership attached: you set product strategy and launch bars for non-deterministic systems yourself, you stay hands-on in product and engineering repos, and you manage, coach and grow a team of product managers doing the same work.

Essential Responsibilities (includes, but is not limited to):

  • Own end-to-end product strategy, roadmap, and launch criteria for the APEX platform surfaces (agent SDK, tool use and orchestration, developer platform, autonomy and trust UX) across a 1-6 quarter horizon; contribute to the portfolio strategy above it
  • Set and own launch-readiness criteria for non-deterministic systems in partnership with Engineering, Security, Research, and Design; make the ship vs hold call yourself
  • Define the autonomy spectrum per capability (human-in-the-loop, AI-assisted, agentic) and the trust and control experience that makes it legible to the people using it
  • Identify and mitigate misuse and risk pre-launch; define the monitoring, audit trail, and rollback that ships with every autonomous capability
  • Personally build prototypes, scripts, and evaluation harnesses to test product decisions, working inside engineering and product repos and internal SDKs as a peer user
  • Be a daily, hands-on user of the platform you own; file precise, implementable bug reports and behavior-change requests
  • Instrument adoption, quality, and safety metrics from day one; run experiments and A/B tests to prove impact rather than assert it
  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of product managers; own development plans and performance conversations for each PM, and raise the craft bar for technical, data-driven product judgment on agentic systems
  • Hire and develop AI-fluent, technically credible product managers; partner with your leader on staffing plans, resourcing needs, and headcount justification
  • Translate vision and portfolio strategy into sequenced, actionable roadmaps tied to business OKRs; own domain-level OKRs and report clearly on progress, risk, and trade-offs
  • Make build/buy/partner decisions for capabilities within APEX, with explicit ROI reasoning
  • Build trusted relationships with peers in Engineering, Design, Data, Security, Marketing, and GTM; secure cross-functional alignment on the APEX strategy and keep it coherent with adjacent domains
  • Ensure responsible AI, ethics, compliance, and legal reviews are completed for products in your domain, following company standards
  • Represent the platform internally and externally: enablement, developer relations, launch communications, and public launches that build credibility for Pax8 in the agentic space
  • Use AI tools and agents in daily work, and model that practice for the team

Skills & Experience:

Core Skills & Experience:

  • At least eight to ten (8 – 10) years of experience in product management or an equivalent role
  • At least three (3) years of experience leading product managers, including experience growing a team
  • Engineering background required: prior professional experience as a software engineer, or an equivalent track record driving technical product direction; comfortable writing code personally at prototype quality (prototypes, scripts, eval harnesses) without handing it to an engineer first
  • Track record delivering product capabilities on a developer-focused platform (APIs, SDKs, CLIs, developer tools), backed by pointable evidence: launch posts, press coverage, changelogs, or documentation you shipped
  • Track record of leading multiple products that drive measurable outcomes, and of leading a significant product, platform, automation, or process transformation
  • Data-driven by nature: designs and runs experiments, instruments adoption and quality metrics from day one, and can show a record of moving them, not just launching features
  • Scrupulous about value for Pax8 and our partners; able to articulate and defend expected ROI
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and people skills; can present a clear narrative to senior leadership
  • Comfortable with ambiguity; adapts quickly and keeps the team oriented when priorities shift

Agentic Platform Depth:

  • Deep, firsthand fluency with how frontier models and agentic systems behave - tool use, planning, multi-step execution, and common failure modes - and with the current agentic platform landscape (agent SDKs, computer-use interfaces, orchestration frameworks)
  • Able to read model evals and capability reports directly and translate them into launch bars, acceptance criteria, and roadmap decisions
  • Sets safety, authority, and escalation boundaries for autonomous capability, and can defend those boundaries to engineering, security, and executive audiences
  • Reached via Breadth (coherence across several interdependent, complex product areas) or Depth (sole expert in one hard, fast-moving product problem) - same level, either route

AI Skills & Experience:

  • Daily experience with tools like Claude, Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Atlassian AI, Figma (design collaboration and AI product research), Pendo (AI product analytics and research collaboration) - with a working view of where each fits in the product workflow
  • Solid understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, including cost, latency, and quality trade-offs
  • Use enterprise-approved AI tools for daily productivity, and redirect the team away from unapproved tools
  • Apply data classification and privacy principles when using AI, and hold the team to the same
  • Practice responsible AI: recognize bias, fairness, and transparency requirements and build them into acceptance criteria
  • Effective prompting and context-setting - clear instructions, context, iterative refinement - and share what works across the team
  • Own the responsible AI ethics review for customer-facing AI products within your domain
  • Measure AI product outcomes: accuracy, user satisfaction, adoption, and business impact
  • Own and apply the company AI standard within your domain: human-in-the-loop, AI-assisted, and agentic decisions are deliberate, documented, and consistently applied
  • AI Proficiency Expectation: Expert

Preferred Skills:

  • Multiple years of professional experience as a software engineer prior to moving into product, beyond the minimum engineering background required above
  • Has personally built agentic evaluations (SWE-bench-style suites, LLM-judge rubrics, model-behavior regression harnesses), not just commissioned them
  • Direct experience with research and design teams as a daily collaborator, not a periodic stakeholder
  • Took a research result or internal prototype into a production product used at scale
  • Defined a new product category or UX pattern with no established precedent (early agentic UX, autonomous coding tools, computer-use interfaces)
  • External visibility in the agentic product space: talks, published product thinking, recognized contribution to industry framing of autonomy, trust, or agent UX

What Success Looks Like:

  • The APEX product vision and strategy are clearly communicated and visibly aligned to business outcomes.
  • Agentic capabilities ship with explicit authority, safety, and escalation boundaries, and with the monitoring, audit trail, and rollback that make them operable.
  • Launch bars for non-deterministic systems are defined, applied consistently, and trusted by Engineering, Security, and executive leadership.
  • Adoption, quality, and safety metrics exist from day one and show measurable movement.
  • Build/buy/partner decisions within the domain are grounded in measurable value.
  • The product management team is AI-fluent, technically credible, well-coached, and growing against clear development plans - with at least one PM ready for the next level.
  • Engineering, Design, Data, Security, and senior stakeholders have clarity on priorities, trade-offs, and delivery expectations.
  • Escalations to your leader are the exception, and they arrive with a recommendation attached.

Compassionate Candour - We aim to assist others with candid, actionable feedback.

Seek to Understand - Be open, curious and committed to learning.

We Before Me - Actively collaborate and seek out diverse perspectives to ensure a win for Team Pax8.

Driven by Passion - Connects personal passion to Pax8 mission, resilient in face of adversity and uncertainty in pursuit of mission.

jobs.excerpt: LOCATION:Remote – must live in or near Vaya’s Western NC region.
jobs.description:
LOCATION:Remote – must live in or near Vaya’s Western NC region. Incumbent in this role must maintain residency in North Carolina or within 40 miles from the NC border. This is a home-based position that requires community travel.

GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

The Transitions to Community Living (TCL) Community Liaison’s primary objectives are to provide education to members/recipients and entities stakeholders about TCL, educating providers on how to identify and report barriers, aid in eliminating barriers, provide and create training opportunities and how to access TCL and via the RSVP (Referral Screening Verification Program) process. This position works with various community stakeholders such as the individual, family, LRPs, community/state hospitals, providers, shelters, and adult care homes. This position will work closely and collaboratively with members of the TCL Team in order to meet the established time frames with requests for required documentation as needed through the process. This position ensures that the specific functions related to the Department of Justice and RSVP are followed. This is a mobile position that will require working in various locations throughout and beyond Vaya Health’s catchment area.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Community Education/Liaison Responsibilities:

A high level of diplomacy and discretion is required to effectively create buy in, negotiate, and resolve concerns or issues, this requires exceptional interpersonal skills, highly effective communication ability, and the propensity to make prompt independent decisions based upon relevant facts. Problem solving, and conflict resolution skills are essential. Demonstrated effective leadership presence is required, with demonstrated confidence in dealing with unknown and complex issues. Awareness of and sensitivity to the complexities of stakeholder and participant concerns.

  • Educate individuals members/recipients and referral entities (hospitals, providers, FCH, ACH, ALF and other key stakeholders) about the TCL eligibility requirements and the RSVP process.
  • Educate and provide training opportunities to internal and external stakeholders regarding TCL program process and how to identify and report barriers.
  • Cascade information to applicable departments within Vaya Health (Vaya) to assist with eliminating TCL barriers
  • Coordinates with referral entities to address and assess the needs of the members/recipients, educate on appropriate services and levels of care as needed.
  • Identifies gaps in services and intervenes to ensure that the individual receives appropriate care, can refer to MHSU Care Management, if appropriate.
  • Ensures that services for the individual are identified and coordinated across the LME/MCO’s system and with other systems, including primary care.
  • Provides education and assistance in collaboration with local hospitals (and other stakeholders) as appropriate to RSVP.
  • While providing outreach and education in the community, the Liaison may also provide potential members/recipients with information on TCL process.
  • Educate facilities stakeholders when members/recipients do not meet TCL eligibility and provide additional community resources when inquiries are received.
  • Other specific functions as they relate to Diversion, In-Reach, Transition Process and Post-Transition responsibilities as indicated from DMA/DMH.
  • Performs related tasks as required.

Collaboration:

  • Collaborates with other members of TCL team and the community to identify areas of need and provides outreach and education in these areas.
  • Serves as a collaborative partner in identifying system barriers. Attends monthly Vaya Local Barriers Committee as a “voting” member to discuss, collaborate and resolve TCL barriers.
  • Sets up, manages, and facilitates meetings with community stakeholders as appropriate to TCL and RSVP process.
  • Facilitates and coordinates the quarterly ACT/CST Collaborative Meeting with assistance across Vaya departments including Quality Management and Provider Network
  • The TCL Community Liaison will work with consumers members/recipients and providers in multiple communities both within and outside the Vaya catchment
  • Works in partnership with other LME/MCO departments to address identified needs within the catchment area.
  • Collects data from concerning TCL via staff report of concerns and collaborates within teams to find resolution of needs.

Documentation:

The TCL Community Liaison is responsible for documenting in an accurate manner that is clear and concise. This documentation will serve to inform the local organization, state, and federal government. Retrieval Operations Lead

Remote

Reveleer delivers a unified platform spanning risk adjustment, quality improvement, clinical intelligence, and member management for health plans and provider organizations navigating the complexity of value-based care. The Retrieval Lead drives frontline execution of Reveleer's retrieval program, covering approximately 500,000 chases beginning with the October 2026 go-live.

This role owns the day-to-day relationship with the program's largest AIDs, distributes and rebalances chase work assignments across the PSR team, and trains new and existing PSRs on retrieval workflows, standard processes, and provider outreach best practices.

This role is the first line of response for provider escalations, resolving access and outreach issues directly and escalating only what requires the Retrieval Manager's involvement.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Large AID Relationship & Provider Contact

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for a program's highest-volume AIDs, maintaining direct relationships with provider office staff.
  • Monitor retrieval performance for large AIDs and proactively address barriers before they affect chase completion.
  • Coordinate directly with provider offices on record request logistics, portal access, and recurring retrieval issues.

Work Assignment & Queue Management

  • Distribute and rebalance daily chase assignments across the PSR team based on AID priority, chase age, and retrieval deadlines.
  • Monitor individual PSR workloads and adjust assignments to keep the queue moving and prevent aged chases from stalling.
  • Partner with the Retrieval Manager on weekly volume planning and flag capacity gaps before they affect throughput.

PSR Training & Development

  • Onboard and train new PSRs on chase workflows, AID ownership, pend code handling, and platform agent hand-offs.
  • Deliver ongoing coaching and refreshers on retrieval best practices, call quality, and documentation standards.
  • Maintain training materials and job aids, updating them as workflows or systems change.

Provider Escalation Management

  • Own first-line resolution of provider escalations related to retrieval outreach, record requests, or access issues.
  • Document escalation patterns and root causes and recommend workflow or script changes that reduce recurring issues.
  • Escalate unresolved or systemic provider issues to the Retrieval Manager with a clear summary and recommend next step.

Performance Monitoring & Coaching

  • Track individual and team-level retrieval rate, pend rate, and productivity against program targets.
  • Provide day-to-day feedback and coaching to PSRs based on chase outcomes and call quality.
  • Flag underperformance or training gaps to the Retrieval Manager and support corrective action plans.

Process Adherence & Documentation

  • Ensure PSR adherence to standard retrieval processes, procedures, and documentation requirements.
  • Maintain accurate, current records on AID assignments, escalation status, and chase ownership.
  • Support the Retrieval Manager with input on process updates and standard operating procedure revisions.

  • 2+ years of experience in healthcare operations, chart retrieval, risk adjustment, or HEDIS/quality program support.

  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage and rebalance work assignments across a team in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency in Excel and comfort working within chase or case management systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience delivering training or coaching.

Preferred

  • Prior experience formally training or onboarding new hires in a call center or retrieval operations setting.

jobs.excerpt: Legal Counsel (m/f/d)Remote EuropeHello 👋 I’m Robert, Finance & Legal Lead at Kayzen and I’m now looking for a Legal Counsel to join our team.
jobs.description:
Legal Counsel (m/f/d)

Remote Europe

Hello 👋 I’m Robert, Finance & Legal Lead at Kayzen and I’m now looking for a Legal Counsel to join our team. As we scale our business globally — managing an increasingly complex client and vendor landscape, navigating cross-border data privacy requirements, and growing our equity and corporate structure — we need a sharp, pragmatic, and commercially minded legal mind to own our legal function. You will take what we have built so far and professionalise, scale, and strengthen it. Working closely with our Finance & Legal Lead, you will be a true business partner to senior leadership across the company.

About Kayzen

Kayzen is an App demand-side platform (DSP) dedicated to democratizing app advertising on Mobile and Connected TV devices. We enable leading apps, agencies, media buyers, and brands to run programmatic customer acquisition, retargeting, and brand performance campaigns through our self-serve and managed service options. Built on the three core pillars of performance, transparency, and control, Kayzen powers the world’s best performance marketing teams with bespoke solutions that fuel business growth and deliver a competitive advantage. With an unprecedented scale of 300B+ daily ad requests from 1.6B+ unique users worldwide, we serve up to 1B+ ads per day in 180 countries. Kayzen is accessible through our APIs and user interface.

The team

You will join a small, senior team and work directly alongside our Finance & Legal Lead. Your key stakeholders will be the leadership team, as well as our Finance, Operations, and Commercial functions across a globally distributed organisation.

The role

As Legal Counsel, you will be Kayzen’s primary legal owner across four core areas. You will operate as a trusted business partner — not just a gatekeeper — and are expected to move fast, apply sound commercial judgment, and help the business scale without unnecessary legal friction.

Responsibilities

GDPR & data privacy compliance

  • Own and continuously develop Kayzen’s GDPR compliance programme as an AdTech company operating across multiple jurisdictions, with a particular focus on EU and US privacy frameworks
  • Advise on data processing agreements, privacy notices, consent frameworks, and cross-border data transfers
  • Act as primary point of contact for internal privacy questions

Transaction advice & contract negotiations

  • Provide legal counsel on T&Cs and related transactions
  • Lead or support contract negotiations with clients and vendors, including MSAs, SaaS agreements, partnership agreements, and NDAs
  • Ensure commercial contracts are legally robust and aligned with company risk appetite

Cap table & corporate law

  • Manage and maintain Kayzen’s cap table
  • Oversee corporate governance across Kayzen’s group structure, including subsidiary management, shareholder resolutions, and notarial filings under German law
  • Support fundraising and investor relations from a legal and corporate perspective

General compliance

  • Further develop and scale Kayzen’s compliance framework to match our growth as an internationally operating company
  • Monitor relevant regulatory developments (ad-tech, data privacy, employment, corporate) and translate them into actionable guidance for the business

Requirements

  • Qualified lawyer (“Volljurist”) or Business lawyer (“Wirtschaftsjurist”) with 2–5 years of relevant professional experience
  • Strong understanding of German business law is essential; additionally solid understanding of international and US legal frameworks, particularly in the context of data privacy and commercial contracts
  • Strong knowledge of GDPR and European data protection law; familiarity with US privacy regulations (CCPA etc.) a strong plus
  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is strongly preferred — you know how to work lean, move fast, and prioritise pragmatically
  • Hands-on experience with contract drafting and commercial negotiations across a variety of agreement types
  • Familiarity with cap table management and corporate governance in a VC-backed or founder-led company context
  • Commercially minded: you understand that good legal advice enables business, not just protects it
  • Fluent in English & German
  • Demonstrated ability to leverage AI tools to enhance legal productivity — you move fast and work smart

What we offer

  • A high-impact legal role with real ownership and room to grow the function
  • Direct collaboration with the Finance & Legal Lead and senior leadership
  • Competitive fixed compensation commensurate with experience
  • Fully remote work arrangement
  • €500 home-office setup budget
  • €1,000 annual learning & development budget
  • A motivated, diverse, and internationally distributed team

GROW WITH US: Tandem Diabetes Care creates new possibilities for people living with diabetes, their loved ones, and their healthcare providers through a positively different experience. We’d love for you to team up with us to “innovate every day,” put “people first,” and take the “no-shortcuts” approach that has propelled us to become a leader in the diabetes technology industry.

STAY AWESOME: Tandem Diabetes Care is proud to manufacture and sell the Tandem Mobi system and t:slim X2 insulin pump with Control-IQ+ technology — an advanced predictive algorithm that automates insulin delivery. But we’re so much more than that. Our company’s human-centered approach to design, development, and support delivers innovative products and services for people who use insulin. Because many of our own team members live with type 1 diabetes, or have a loved one impacted by diabetes, the work is personal, and we are committed to the cause. Learn more at tandemdiabetes.com

A DAY IN THE LIFE:

At Tandem Diabetes Care, we are creating new possibilities for people living with diabetes, their loved ones, and healthcare providers through a positively different experience.

We are looking for a Demand Planer Manager to join our International team. This role is based in the Netherlands and offers a remote working arrangement. The successful candidate should be willing and able to travel regularly to other international locations as required to support business needs.
In this influential role, you will lead demand planning, forecasting, inventory allocation, and operational coordination across Tandem’s international distributor and direct markets. You will help align customer demand, product availability, revenue expectations, and fulfilment plans while strengthening the processes and partnerships that support our continued international growth.

STAY AWESOME:

Tandem is dedicated to making diabetes technology more intuitive, innovative, and human. We combine advanced technology with a personal connection to our mission, always keeping the needs of people living with diabetes at the heart of what we do.

As our Demand Planer Manager, you will turn market insights and commercial priorities into clear, actionable demand plans. Working across Commercial, Supply Chain, Finance, Operations, Marketing, Regulatory, and distributor partners, you will help identify risks early, optimise inventory, and ensure international markets are ready for product launches and changing customer needs.

A DAY IN THE LIFE:

In this role, you will:

  • Own the monthly demand planning and forecasting process for Tandem’s international distributor partners and direct markets.

  • Consolidate market forecasts and analyse forecast accuracy, bias, demand variability, purchasing patterns, and emerging trends.

  • Establish effective planning rhythms, including monthly reviews with direct markets and quarterly demand reviews with distributor partners.

  • Lead and participate in S&OP discussions covering demand, inventory health, service levels, purchasing patterns, and operational risks.

  • Build strong partnerships with country leadership and distributor teams to gather real-time market intelligence, commercial insights, competitive developments, tender opportunities, and launch information.

  • Challenge assumptions and investigate material forecast changes, demand spikes, demand erosion, inventory imbalances, and unusual ordering trends.

  • Create consensus demand plans that balance market expectations, inventory availability, supply constraints, financial objectives, and operational capabilities.

  • Align forecasts with open orders, shipment plans, product availability, and fulfilment expectations in partnership with Operations Specialists, Logistics, Fulfilment, and Supply Chain.

  • Support new product introductions, software releases, product enhancements, and discontinuations by developing market-specific forecasts, inventory strategies, and transition plans.

  • Identify ageing, excess, or potentially obsolete inventory and work with international markets to develop mitigation and depletion strategies.

  • Lead demand allocation planning during supply-constrained situations, taking account of customer impact, tender commitments, launches, available inventory, and market requirements.

  • Partner with Finance on revenue planning and help develop dashboards and reporting covering forecast performance, inventory exposure, order trends, and revenue projections.

  • Present demand, inventory, and fulfilment insights to Commercial and Operations leadership.

  • Improve planning tools, reporting, operational workflows, automation, and analytics to increase forecast accuracy and operational efficiency.

jobs.excerpt: About the RoleAbnormal AI is seeking a Product Manager (Outbound) who builds the field motion from the ground up for every new product launched.
jobs.description:
About the Role

Abnormal AI is seeking a Product Manager (Outbound) who builds the field motion from the ground up for every new product launched. There is no universal playbook, no inherited demo flow, and no proven messaging to hand off. Each new product requires its own: this person architects it, validates it in close partnership with the field, and hands off a repeatable motion the field can run at scale before moving to the next product launch.

Outbound Product Management (OPM) is R&D's operating layer in the field, the function that sits between what we build and how it performs with customers. That means being first in on a new product, before anyone has figured out how to sell or demo it, running structured validation across customer accounts, and distinguishing a product gap from a positioning or sales-motion gap. You'll work in close partnership with Product Management and Product Marketing—OPM owns the field motion, not the roadmap, but the pattern analysis and positioning work you bring back is what keeps both teams calibrated to what's actually happening with customers.

This is not a feedback-intake role. You'll be operating on products that don't have established answers yet — the messaging is still being proven, the competitive positioning is still being tested, and the product itself may still be taking shape. You'll know when a read is solid enough to bring back to the cross-functional team versus when it needs more digging, and you'll drive the motion forward without waiting for someone to hand you a map.

What You'll Do

  • Architect the field motion for an assigned product launch: design how the product gets demoed, how a POV gets structured, and what the field needs to run it at scale — then get hands-on with customer discovery, deep dives, and POVs to validate the approach.
  • Test and refine messaging hypotheses in live deals alongside Sales Engineers, and diagnose competitive loss reasons.
  • Brief PM with pattern analysis across accounts, distinguishing a product gap from a positioning or sales-motion problem.
  • Partner with Product Marketing as a standing collaborator, stress-testing messaging in live deals and reporting what's landing versus what needs to change.
  • Own the handoff at General Availability: document what worked, what broke, and what the field needs to run the motion independently — then move to the next product and do it again.

Must-Have Skills

  • 5+ years in Product Management or Solutions/Sales Engineering in enterprise security.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently synthesize unfamiliar products quickly — given a new product and limited context, you can identify what matters, form a hypothesis, and start building the field motion: how the product gets demoed, how a POV gets structured, and what the field needs to run it at scale.
  • Experience working in a pre-launch or early-stage product environment before a playbook existed, with a specific program, motion, or deliverable built from scratch to show for it.
  • Credibility that speaks through work and presence, and the instinct to move toward problems before they're assigned.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; credible in front of technical buyers and security teams, equally comfortable in a live customer conversation and an internal roadmap review.
  • High operational excellence and ownership: you've taken a field observation from raw signal to a documented recommendation that a PM or GTM team acted on.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the capacity to reason through ambiguous problems and move to a working hypothesis without waiting for the full picture.

Nice to Have

  • Prior involvement in new product launches, design partnerships, early-access, and/or beta programs.
  • Experience running or presenting in structured cross-functional forums (POV reviews, launch/GTM syncs).
  • Familiarity with enterprise security platforms such as CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Wiz, Microsoft, or similar.
  • Comfort using AI tools to synthesize patterns across large sets of qualitative input (support tickets, call transcripts, win/loss notes).
  • Prior startup experience.

Why This Role Matters

This role is a career inflection point. It’s a senior seat with real organizational weight that will set a new standard for the team around you. The people who thrive here carry credibility on arrival—they've been in enough high-stakes customer and cross-functional environments that they don't need to win the room before the work begins. If you come from a product management background, this is where you build the GTM fluency that traditional PM roles don't give you, and that fluency is increasingly what separates good product people from exceptional ones. If you come from a solutions engineering background, this is where technical credibility becomes strategic ownership. Either way, you'll be at the frontier of what we're building, working on products that don't have all the answers yet, shaping the motion before anyone else has, and coming out the other side with a profile that's genuinely hard to replicate elsewhere. The launches you'll be working on aren't side bets—they're the company's biggest bets for our next phase of growth, and this role is at the center of bringing them to market.

Actual compensation will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location.
In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Vendor Contract Negotiations

Public-Facing Privacy and Trust Documentation

  • Develop and maintain customer-facing privacy, data-use, security, and compliance materials.

Policies, Playbooks, and Legal Enablement
