jobs.excerpt: About ValsoftValsoft builds and scales vertical market software companies.
jobs.description:
About Valsoft

Valsoft builds and scales vertical market software companies. We partner with strong teams, invest in the long term, and run disciplined operating systems to drive sustainable growth across our portfolio.

About BluSynq

BluSynq is changing the way operators run their front desk. Our AI-powered agent connects to the tools a business already uses and answers questions, books appointments and closes deals — automatically, 24/7 — over voice, text and email. We are a fast-scaling, tech-driven business inside the Valsoft / Aspire Software portfolio, working closely with DockMaster, the leading marina management platform.

The Opportunity

This is a first or second sales job, and a real one.

We're hiring a Junior Account Executive to take BluSynq into new markets.

BluSynq already has a natural home inside DockMaster's marina customer base. That is not your territory. Yours is everything outside it: independent operators who have never heard of us, and the adjacent industries where the same problem exists. If a business loses money every time the phone rings and nobody picks up, it's a prospect.

You won't be doing it alone. A dedicated Sales Development Representative works alongside you, building target lists and running first-touch outreach to book qualified meetings into your calendar. From that first meeting on, the deal is yours: discovery, demo, proposal, negotiation and close.

You'll still create pipeline of your own. The best sellers always do, and in a new market a rep who only works booked meetings never learns why the market says no. But you have a partner at the top of the funnel, and a real say in who they call.

You will not be building the go-to-market strategy. That's the point. The talk tracks, demo flow, pricing and CRM process are being built for you by the senior seller and the COO. What you will do is find out which industries outside our home market actually buy — and that read is worth as much to us as the revenue.

You'll be coached directly, weekly, on live calls and recorded ones. If you're hungry, coachable and willing to pick up the phone yourself when the calendar looks thin, this is a seat where you can be closing your own deals inside 60 days and running a full territory inside a year.

Where You'll Sell

Every deal you close is a net-new logo. You'll work two fronts:

  • The marine market we don't already serve — independent marinas, boatyards, yacht clubs, waterfront venues and dealerships that are not DockMaster customers.
  • Adjacent industries with the same front-desk problem — appointment-driven, phone-dependent, owner-operated businesses, including:
  • RV parks, campgrounds and glamping sites
  • Self-storage and boat/RV storage facilities
  • Marine and powersports dealerships and their service departments
  • Entertainment attractions, waterparks and event venues
  • Home and field services — HVAC, plumbing, landscaping, pool service

– Auto service and repair shops

  • Clinics, veterinary practices, salons and spas

Part of the job is proving which of these are real. You and your SDR will run structured tests in new verticals, two at a time, and report back on what lands and what doesn't. Any prospect that turns out to be a DockMaster customer gets routed to the DockMaster team — those accounts are covered separately, and the rules of engagement will be written down for you before day one.

What You'll Do

Work with your SDR to open new markets

  • Partner daily with your SDR: agree the target account criteria, review the lists they build in ZoomInfo and LinkedIn, listen to their calls, and tell them what is landing so the meetings get better.
  • Accept, qualify or reject every meeting they book against criteria you have both signed up to — with feedback either way, same day. That loop is how the top of the funnel improves.
  • Self-source a meaningful share of your own pipeline — phone, email, LinkedIn and the occasional trade show — so you are never dependent on someone else's calendar.
  • Research every account before the call, so the first 20 seconds are about their business and not about us.
  • Learn a new industry's vocabulary fast enough to sound credible to an operator who has run that business for twenty years.
  • Log every touch in HubSpot the same day, tagged by vertical and lead source. Clean CRM is how we tell a good market from a bad one, and SDR-sourced from self-sourced.

Own the sales cycle

  • Own every deal from the first meeting to signature. Once a lead is handed to you, it is yours — the forecast, the follow-up and the outcome.
  • Run discovery calls using our qualification framework, and get to the operator's actual problem: missed calls, after-hours bookings, staff time lost to the phone.
  • Deliver the BluSynq demo and connect what the prospect just heard to time saved and revenue captured.
  • Build and send proposals, handle standard objections, and close.
  • Hand new customers to Onboarding and Customer Success cleanly, with the context they need to get the customer live fast.

Report back and get better every week

  • Come to your 1:1 with your numbers, your recorded calls and the one thing you want to fix.
  • Give a clear read on each vertical you test: who answered, what landed, what they pushed back on, whether it's worth more of our time.
  • Feed real objections, competitive mentions and pricing pushback back to the team so the playbook improves.
  • Contribute to talk tracks and sequences once you've earned an opinion by making the calls.

Ramp and Expectations

First 30 days — learn the product and pick your ground

  • Certified on the BluSynq demo and able to deliver it unassisted.
  • Two target verticals agreed with the COO and your SDR, with lists built and outbound live in both.
  • A working rhythm established with your SDR: shared qualification criteria, a weekly list review and a same-day feedback loop on every meeting booked.
  • HubSpot hygiene at 100%: every activity logged, every next step dated, every account tagged by vertical.

Days 31–60 — run the cycle

  • Consistently hitting weekly activity targets and holding a live discovery calendar.
  • Running your own demos and building qualified pipeline in both test verticals.
  • Converting SDR-booked meetings at or above our benchmark, with self-sourced opportunities on top.

• First closed deal on the board.

  • An early, evidence-based read on which of the two verticals is responding.

Days 61–90 — carry a number

  • Full quota carrying, with 3x pipeline coverage against it.
  • A repeatable weekly rhythm: SDR review, self-sourced prospecting, discover, demo, propose, close.
  • Hitting the agreed self-sourced share of pipeline alongside SDR-sourced volume.
  • A documented view of which verticals convert, which to drop, and a third in test.
  • Forecasting your own deals accurately enough that we can plan around them.

KPIs you'll be measured on

  • Discovery calls held per week at full ramp: 8–10 across SDR-booked and self-sourced.
  • Self-sourced outbound activity: ~25 quality touches a day, including live cold dials.
  • Share of your pipeline you sourced yourself, against a ratio agreed in week one.
  • Speed and quality of your feedback loop with the SDR — every booked meeting dispositioned same day.
  • New-logo closes and new ARR — all of it net-new, none of it from the DockMaster base.
  • Demo-to-close conversion against a team benchmark you'll be given in week one.
  • Verticals tested per quarter, with a written read on each.
  • Pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy and CRM data quality.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 0–2 years of experience in a sales, customer-facing or target-driven role. A first sales job is welcome.
  • Genuinely comfortable making a cold call — no referral, no inbound form, no existing relationship.
  • Resilient about rejection, because opening a new market means a lot of it before the first yes.
  • Clear, confident communicator — on the phone, on video and in writing.
  • Coachable: you take feedback, apply it the same week, and ask for more.
  • Willing to be a partner to your SDR rather than a passenger — giving them direction and feedback, not just taking their meetings.
  • Organised and self-directed enough to run your own day in a remote role without someone counting your hours.
  • Curious about how different kinds of businesses actually operate, and interested in getting good at software sales as a craft.
  • Legally able to work in Canada and available to work North American business hours.

Preferred

  • Any exposure to cold outbound — SDR/BDR work, retail, hospitality, call centre, recruiting, fundraising, or another role where you had a number and a script.
  • Experience selling into more than one industry, or into small owner-operated businesses where the buyer is the owner.
  • Experience with a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce or similar) and prospecting tools like ZoomInfo — helpful, not required. We'll teach it.
  • Familiarity with marinas, boating, RV parks, campgrounds, storage, dealerships or another owner-operator business. Knowing the customer is worth more here than knowing SaaS.
  • Interest in AI and automation, and the ability to explain it to someone who doesn't care how it works — only what it does for them.

What We're Not Asking For

  • SaaS experience. We'd rather have a fast learner with the right instincts than someone with three years of bad habits.
  • A university degree in anything specific.
  • An existing book of business or industry contacts.

Why Join

  • You're not farming someone else's customer list. Every logo you close is a new one.
  • You have a dedicated SDR feeding the top of your funnel from day one — rare in a first AE seat — and you own the deal from the first meeting onward.
  • Sell a product prospects can hear working in the first two minutes of a demo, in markets that haven't been called on yet.
  • Real influence in your first year on which industries BluSynq goes after next — your data decides it.
  • Short sales cycles: you'll get more at-bats in a year here than in three years selling enterprise software, which is how sellers actually get good.
  • Direct, weekly coaching from a senior seller and the COO — not a 40-person SDR floor.
  • A defined path: this seat is built to grow into a full Account Executive territory, with clear milestones rather than a vague promise.
  • Competitive base salary with uncapped commission.
  • Backed by Valsoft / Aspire Software — the stability of a global portfolio with the pace and ownership of a startup.

Position Summary:

The Senior Buyer is responsible for sourcing and purchasing materials, components, fabricated products, and services supporting the company’s manufacturing and distribution operations. This role will focus on products and engineered solutions sold to data-center customers, including air compressors, pumps, valves, piping systems, fabricated skids, and related equipment. The successful candidate will have extensive purchasing experience in both manufacturing and distribution environments, strong knowledge of ERP and material-planning systems, and the technical ability to understand engineered products, drawings, specifications, bills of material, and customer requirements. This position will work closely with Engineering, Operations, Sales, Quality, Inventory Management, and suppliers to ensure materials are available at the right cost, quality, and delivery performance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Source and purchase air compressors, pumps, valves, piping components, fabricated skids, motors, controls, instrumentation, and related materials used in data-center applications.
  • Manage purchasing activities for both stocked distribution products and engineered-to-order manufacturing projects.
  • Review customer requirements, bills of material, engineering drawings, specifications, and production schedules to determine material requirements.
  • Issue requests for quotation, analyze supplier proposals, negotiate pricing and commercial terms, and issue purchase orders.
  • Develop sourcing strategies that improve product availability, reduce total cost, shorten lead times, and strengthen supply-chain continuity.
  • Work closely with Engineering and Project Management to source technically compliant components for custom skid packages and integrated systems.
  • Monitor purchase orders, supplier acknowledgments, production schedules, and delivery commitments to ensure materials arrive on time.
  • Identify potential material shortages, long-lead-time items, and supply risks before they affect customer delivery or manufacturing schedules.
  • Maintain accurate purchasing data within the ERP system, including supplier information, pricing, lead times, order quantities, and delivery dates.
  • Use ERP-generated demand, inventory levels, forecasts, customer orders, and production requirements to make purchasing decisions.
  • Balance inventory availability with working-capital objectives, stocking policies, customer demand, and service-level expectations.
  • Negotiate supplier pricing, payment terms, freight terms, warranties, stocking agreements, and other commercial conditions.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with manufacturers, distributors, fabricators, and strategic supply partners.
  • Evaluate supplier performance based on quality, delivery, cost, responsiveness, and technical capability.
  • Participate in supplier business reviews, corrective-action activities, and supplier-development initiatives.
  • Collaborate with Quality Assurance to resolve supplier nonconformances, defective materials, documentation issues, and corrective actions.
  • Support cost-reduction, value-engineering, standardization, and supplier-consolidation initiatives.
  • Assist Sales and Estimating with supplier quotations, material costs, lead times, and sourcing strategies for data-center opportunities.
  • Ensure purchasing activities comply with company policies, contractual requirements, customer specifications, and applicable quality standards.
  • Maintain appropriate purchasing documentation, supplier records, quotations, certifications, and audit trails.
  • Perform other supply-chain and purchasing responsibilities as assigned.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline required.
  • Minimum of seven years of progressive purchasing, sourcing, or supply-chain experience.
  • Demonstrated purchasing experience within both manufacturing and distribution environments.
  • Experience sourcing industrial equipment and components such as air compressors, pumps, valves, piping, controls, instrumentation, fabricated assemblies, or skid-mounted systems strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting data-center, mission-critical infrastructure, industrial construction, mechanical systems, or engineered-project customers preferred.
  • Experience purchasing materials for engineered-to-order, configured-to-order, or project-based manufacturing operations preferred.

Required Knowledge and Skills:

  • Strong working knowledge of ERP, MRP, purchasing, inventory-management, and material-planning systems.
  • Ability to use ERP data to evaluate demand, supply, inventory, lead times, safety stock, open orders, and material availability.
  • Strong understanding of purchasing principles, strategic sourcing, supplier management, contract terms, and total cost of ownership.
  • Ability to read and interpret bills of material, technical specifications, engineering drawings, and product documentation.
  • Strong negotiation, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, suppliers, and projects simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.
  • Ability to work effectively across Sales, Engineering, Manufacturing, Distribution, Quality, Finance, and Project Management.
  • Strong sense of urgency and the ability to respond effectively to changing customer and production requirements.
  • Knowledge of data-center mechanical infrastructure and mission-critical equipment is highly desirable.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Professional certification such as CPSM, CPIM, CSCP, or CPM.
  • Experience with supplier scorecards, contract negotiations, cost modeling, and commodity strategies.
  • Knowledge of lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and inventory-optimization principles.

Job Title: Virtual CRA Info Session - 11.4.2026 (Clinical Research Coordinator Experience)

Job Location: UNAVAILABLE, United States

Job Seniority Level:

Medpace will be hosting a Virtual Networking Event to highlight our exciting Clinical Research Associate opportunites! We are seeking qualified Clinical Research Coordinators and Research Nurses to attend.

When: Wednesday, November 4th from 6-7pm ET on Microsoft Teams.

*More details regarding the format of this virtual event will be provided should you be selected to attend.

Clinical Research Coordinators/Research Nurses wanted at Medpace! Become a CRA and join our growing team!

This is an exciting opportunity for clinical research professionals with at least 2 years of Clinical Research Coordinator experience to fill Clinical Research Associate (CRA) openings at Medpace. Through our PACE® Training Program, you will receive the training needed to become a fully functional CRA with the opportunity to work home-based. You will also have the opportunity to earn a generous travel bonus in addition to a competitive salary.

WE OFFER THE FOLLOWING

  • Competitive travel bonus;
  • Equity/Stock Option program;
  • Training completion and retention bonus
  • Annual merit increases;
  • 401K matching;
  • The opportunity to work from home;
  • Flexible work hours across days within a week;
  • Retain airline reward miles and hotel reward points;
  • Home office furniture allowance, laptop, mobile phone with hotspot for internet access anywhere;
  • In-house travel agents and reimbursement for airline club;
  • Opportunity for leadership positions – Lead CRA, CRA Manager, Clinical Trial Manager, Training and Development Manager, and many more;
  • CRA training program (PACE®);
  • Ongoing therapeutic training by our in-house physicians who are medical and regulatory experts;
  • In-house administrative support for all levels of CRAs; and
  • Opportunities to work with international team of CRAs.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct qualification, initiation, monitoring, and closeout visits at research sites in compliance with the approved protocol;
  • Communication with the medical site staff including coordinators, clinical research physicians, and their site staff;
  • Verify adequate investigator qualifications, training and resources, including facilities, laboratories, equipment, and staff;
  • Medical record and research source documentation verification against case report form data, including informing the site staff of any entry errors, ensuring good documentation practices are being adhered to and communicating protocol deviations appropriately per SOPs, GCP, and applicable regulatory requirements;
  • On-site and virtual/remote monitoring activities with a risk-based monitoring approach (including centralized data review) through our integrated Clinical Trial Management System to identify site deviations/deficiencies and corrective/preventive actions to bring a site back into compliance and mitigate risks moving forward;
  • Verification that the investigator is enrolling only eligible subjects;
  • Regulatory document review;
  • Medical device and/or investigational product/drug accountability and inventory;
  • Verification and review of adverse events, serious adverse events, concomitant medications and corresponding illnesses to confirm accurate data reporting in accordance with the protocol;
  • Assess the clinical research site’s patient recruitment and retention success and offering suggestions for improvement; and
  • Completion of monitoring reports and follow-up letters, which includes providing summaries of the significant findings, deviations, deficiencies, and recommended actions to secure compliance.

Qualifications

  • Must have a minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in a health or science related field;
  • Experience as a Clinical Research Coordinator (minimum 2 years);
  • Ability to travel 60-70% to locations nationwide is required; some visits may be conducted remotely;
  • Must maintain a valid driver’s license and the ability to drive to monitoring sites;
  • Proficient knowledge of Microsoft® Office;
  • Strong communication and presentation skills; and
  • Must be detail-oriented and efficient in time management.

Medpace Overview

Medpace is a full-service clinical contract research organization (CRO) providing phase l-lV clinical development services to the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and medical device industries. Our mission is to accelerate the global development of safe and effective medical therapeutics through the advancement of clinical research. We leverage in-country regulatory and therapeutic expertise across all major therapeutic areas including oncology, cardiology, metabolic, endocrinology, central nervous system, and anti-viral and anti-infective. Headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, we employ more than 6,500 people across 40+ countries.


Why Medpace?

When you join Medpace, you become part of an innovative team that brings cutting-edge therapies to market while building a meaningful and rewarding career focused on scientific excellence and improving patient outcomes around the world through continuous learning and cross-functional collaboration.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.excerpt: Thanks for your interest in Oklo!  We are searching for a Technical Program Manager to join Oklo's Recycling Division.
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Technical Program Manager to join Oklo's Recycling Division. We are looking to fill this role immediately.

Position Description

The Technical Program Manager will lead the development and execution of technical projects with U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories and other government partners, turning strategic opportunities into well-defined agreements, work packages, and delivered results.

The Technical Program Manager will serve as the primary point of contact and, where appropriate, principal investigator for national laboratory collaborations. You will work across Recycling engineering teams and interface closely with Legal, Procurement, Finance, and Recycling leadership to negotiate, establish, and execute contracts, cooperative agreements, and related project mechanisms.

This role is for a technically fluent program leader who can develop new opportunities, shape ambiguous ideas into executable projects, and manage complex external partnerships from concept through closeout. Success requires strong technical judgment grounded in relevant experience, disciplined delivery management, and the ability to navigate technical, contractual, financial, and legal considerations in a fast-moving, highly regulated environment.

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Serve as Oklo's primary point of contact and, as assigned, principal investigator for national laboratory projects and other government-funded collaborations related to spent nuclear fuel recycling and pyroprocessing technology.
  • Develop and manage project scope, statements of work, work packages, budgets, schedules, roles, success criteria, and acceptance criteria with national laboratory partners.
  • Lead negotiations and coordinate internal approvals for contracts, subcontracts, cooperative agreements, Strategic Partnership Projects, CRADAs, DOE funding agreements, and other collaboration mechanisms.
  • Collaborate with laboratory partners and internal technical teams to develop collaborative project content, including technical objectives, work plans, deliverables, intellectual property considerations, contracting avenues, and resource commitments.
  • Interface with Legal, Procurement, Finance, and Recycling leadership to establish agreements and resolve contractual, financial, intellectual property, compliance, and execution issues.
  • Manage contract deliverables, technical reports, milestones, invoices, funding profiles, action items, and overall work delivery through project completion and closeout.
  • Maintain clear project governance, decision rights, meeting cadence, risk and issue tracking, change control, and communication across Oklo and laboratory teams.
  • Monitor partner performance and project health; identify scope, schedule, cost, legal, or technical issues early and drive timely resolution or escalation.
  • Develop new collaboration opportunities by translating Recycling Division needs and strategic priorities into project concepts suitable for national laboratory or DOE engagement.
  • Solicit, evaluate, and mature project proposals from internal Recycling teams, coordinating leadership prioritization and partner engagement.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience in technical project or program management, national laboratory engagement, government contracting, research administration, engineering management, or a related role.
  • Experience managing complex, cross-functional technical projects involving external partners, contractual deliverables, budgets, schedules, and milestones.
  • Experience developing scopes of work, work packages, project plans, reports, or other formal technical deliverables.
  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, physical science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate Legal, Procurement, Finance, technical teams, and leadership to establish and execute agreements.
  • Strong project controls and organizational skills, including the ability to manage multiple agreements, deadlines, funding constraints, and stakeholder commitments concurrently.
  • Experience identifying funding opportunities, developing project concepts or proposals, and building collaborative relationships with government and laboratory stakeholders.
  • Comfort operating in a matrixed environment, influencing without direct authority, and working through ambiguity.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical, contractual, financial, and legal considerations clearly to different audiences.

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience collaborating with DOE national laboratories or DOE offices and programs, including DOE-NE, DOE-ID, DOE-OSO, ARPA-E, DOE-SC, DOE-OTT, or DOE-NNSA.
  • Experience developing or administering Cooperative Research and Development Agreements (CRADAs), Strategic Partnership Projects, interagency agreements, grants, cooperative agreements, subcontracts, or similar mechanisms.
  • Familiarity with government contracting, intellectual property, export control, data rights, compliance, and other legal considerations associated with research and development partnerships.
  • Technical experience in nuclear energy, fuel cycle, chemical processing, advanced manufacturing, or another highly regulated engineering environment.

Competencies

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager who is:

  • An excellent communicator: Clear, concise, and credible; able to align technical, commercial, legal, and leadership stakeholders around decisions and actions.
  • Technically fluent and curious: Comfortable engaging with engineering and research details to understand objectives, assumptions, interfaces, risks, and deliverables.
  • Execution-oriented: Skilled at converting opportunities into scoped agreements, accountable owners, measurable milestones, and sustained follow-through.
  • Commercially and contractually aware: Able to recognize how scope, funding, intellectual property, data rights, and agreement terms affect project execution.
  • A systems thinker: Able to connect laboratory work with Recycling Division priorities and understand how technical, contractual, financial, and organizational decisions interact.
  • Collaborative and influential: Builds trust with laboratory partners and internal teams and drives alignment and closure without depending on formal authority.
  • Entrepreneurial and adaptable: Proactively identifies opportunities, shapes new project concepts, and remains effective when requirements or funding paths are still emerging.
  • Strategic and detail-oriented: Connects individual agreements and deliverables to the broader Recycling strategy while maintaining disciplined control of commitments and deadlines.
  • Mission- and safety-driven: Motivated to advance first-of-a-kind nuclear technology while maintaining technical rigor, compliance, and strong stewardship of public and company resources.

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $120,000-$180,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

The Perks:

As recognized members of the Cyber Elite, we work together in partnership to defend our nation’s critical infrastructure while building meaningful and exciting career development opportunities in a culture tailored to the individual’s technical and professional growth. We are committed to the belief that our team members do their best work when they are happy and well cared for. Highlighted benefits include 144 hours of PTO, 11 holidays, 85% of insurance premiums covered, a 401(k), continuing education, certification maintenance and reimbursement and more.

Who we’re looking for:

We are seeking a Lead Security Architect who possesses deep technical mastery in designing resilient, enterprise-grade security frameworks. You will serve as the strategic visionary and technical anchor, ensuring our mission-critical systems are inherently secure by design and aligned with evolving federal defense standards. In this role, the Lead Security Architect will bridge the gap between complex engineering requirements and executive risk management orchestrating the transition to a robust Zero Trust environment. This is a unique opportunity to shape the growth, development and culture of an exciting and fast-growing company in the cybersecurity market.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead the design and evaluation of enterprise security architectures, ensuring all systems align with Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles and organizational cybersecurity guidelines.
  • Serve as the primary technical liaison between enterprise architects and systems security engineers to ensure security controls are correctly allocated and implemented.
  • Convert complex operational needs and stakeholder security interests into detailed technical requirements and functional specifications.
  • Provide critical input to the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process, including the development of system life-cycle support plans and operational procedures.
  • Manage security requirements throughout the acquisition life cycle, from drafting statements of work to evaluating vendor-proposed security designs for adequacy.
  • Perform regular security reviews and design modeling to identify architecture gaps, developing comprehensive risk management plans to address vulnerabilities.
  • Categorize systems and define clear security boundaries, documenting the protection needs for information systems and networks.
  • Advise senior leadership and authorized officials on design concepts, project costs and the potential adverse effects of identified vulnerabilities.

What you need to know:

  • Deep proficiency in describing and documenting IT architectures using frameworks such as TOGAF, DoDAF or FEAF, with a focus on integrating security into the full system development life cycle.
  • Mastery of Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles, including identity management (PKI, Oauth, SAML), micro-segmentation and secure cloud/hybrid IT delivery models like DevOps and Agile.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of NIST 800-series, FedRAMP and the Risk Management Framework (RMF) to ensure systems meet stringent federal and defense cybersecurity standards.
  • Technical expertise in network security (TCP/IP, VPNs, firewalls), encryption algorithms and the ability to design countermeasures against complex cyber threats and vulnerabilities.
  • Ability to translate operational requirements into technical protection needs and effectively communicate risk and design concepts to both technical experts and executive stakeholders.

Must have’s:

  • 10+ years of professional experience in cybersecurity, including 5+ years in security architecture or a senior technical role
  • One or more of the following certifications: (ISC)2 Certified Information Security Professional (CISSP), GIAC Security Enterprise Architect (GSEA) or GIAC Defensible Security Architecture (GDSA).
  • Proven ability to analyze complex requirements and translate them into clear, actionable tasks and processes through critical thinking.
  • Demonstrated experience architecting secure enterprise systems using Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles.
  • Applicants must be a U.S. citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance, in compliance with federal contract requirements.

À propos du Collège des consultants en immigration et en citoyenneté (le Collège)

Le Collège est l’autorité mandatée par le gouvernement du Canada pour réglementer la pratique des consultants réglementés en immigration canadienne (CRIC) et des conseillers réglementés en immigration pour étudiants étrangers (CRIEE). Son rôle et ses pouvoirs sont établis dans la Loi sur le Collège des consultants en immigration et en citoyenneté (Canada). Le Collège établit les normes de la profession en matière de délivrance de permis, de formation et d’éthique et veille à leur application dans l’intérêt public.

Secteur Organisme d’autoréglementation (OAR)

TITRE DU POSTE : Enquêteur ou enquêteuse

Service : Conduite professionnelle

Supérieur immédiat : Superviseur·e, enquêtes

Exigences linguistiques : Bilinguisme non essentiel

Lieu : Canada

Classification : Poste contractuel de 12 mois

Pourquoi vous joindre à nous?

Souhaitez-vous faire partie d’une équipe qui a à cœur de renforcer et de soutenir la profession de consultant en immigration et en citoyenneté? Si vous partagez notre passion et notre objectif, posez votre candidature ci-dessous pour vous joindre à une équipe qui apporte une contribution importante.

De quelle façon ce rôle soutiendra-t-il notre équipe?

Le titulaire du poste fait enquête sur les plaintes pour manquement professionnel d’une manière impartiale et professionnelle tout en assurant la transparence et l’efficience du processus, ainsi que la protection du public.

Les responsabilités comprennent les éléments suivants (sans toutefois s’y limiter)

  • Examiner les plaintes afin d’évaluer les risques et cerner les problèmes potentiels liés à la conduite en vertu du Code de déontologie du Collège, du Règlement administratif et de la loi.
  • Enquêter sur les plaintes et allégations relatives au manquement professionnel.
  • Recueillir, interpréter, documenter et conserver les renseignements et les éléments de preuve pertinents. Il peut s’agir d’obtenir des citations à comparaître et des mandats.
  • Mener des entrevues avec les plaignants, les témoins et les titulaires de permis afin d’aider le conseiller juridique, le Comité des plaintes et le Comité de discipline à établir les faits de l’affaire en cause.
  • Assurer la liaison avec d’autres parties prenantes, incluant les membres du public, les conseillers juridiques, les membres du Tribunal et les organismes d’application de la loi afin de recueillir des renseignements supplémentaires.
  • Assurer la liaison avec les titulaires de permis et leurs conseillers juridiques dans le but d’obtenir les dossiers clients, les communications et les documents pertinents dans le cadre d'une enquête.
  • Préparer les documents d’enquête et le rapport d’enquête final qui seront soumis aux membres de l’équipe ou du comité appropriés.
  • Fournir du soutien dans le cadre du processus d’audience en préparant et révisant les documents en prévision des audiences et en témoignant dans le cadre d’audiences disciplinaires, si nécessaire.
  • Collaborer avec d’autres membres du personnel afin de cerner les tendances et les pratiques exigeant une enquête plus approfondie (p. ex. les stratagèmes frauduleux et les cas de récidive).

Ce rôle soutiendra notre équipe en y apportant les éléments suivants

  • Pensée critique et capacité d’analyse permettant d’analyser la preuve et d’en tirer des conclusions
  • Aptitudes pour la gestion du temps et sens de l’organisation permettant de gérer et de hiérarchiser des priorités et des échéances concurrentes
  • Sens de l’organisation permettant de gérer les échéances et un volume élevé de documents et de dossiers liés aux cas
  • Souplesse permettant de travailler dans un environnement au rythme rapide et changeant en faisant preuve d’un esprit d’équipe et d’initiative
  • Aptitudes pour la gestion des relations interpersonnelles et des relations avec les parties prenantes permettant de désamorcer une situation et d’interagir de manière professionnelle et respectueuse avec les parties prenantes (titulaires de permis, témoins, etc.) qui éprouvent souvent du stress, de l’inquiétude ou de la colère face à l’affaire en cause
  • Aptitudes pour la communication écrite et verbale permettant de préparer les dossiers relatifs aux cas (p. ex. rapports de plainte, résumés des entrevues et affidavits), de témoigner dans le cadre d’audiences disciplinaires et de communiquer avec diplomatie et respect avec des parties qui font souvent face à des barrières linguistiques
  • Souci du détail permettant de veiller à l’exactitude et à l’exhaustivité de l’examen des documents et des dossiers
  • Tact et discrétion afin de traiter des questions de nature confidentielle et sensible

Formation et expérience requises

  • Diplôme collégial dans un domaine connexe comme les affaires, le risque, l’immigration, le droit ou l’application de la loi, en plus d’autres formations ou certificats dans une discipline connexe (p. ex. fraude, enquête)
  • Trois à cinq années d’expérience dans un poste lié aux enquêtes au sein d’un organisme de réglementation ou d’application de la loi
  • Connaissance des processus d’enquête, des règles de preuve et de l’évaluation de la preuve, ainsi que des techniques d’entrevue, des cyberenquêtes et des méthodes qui s’y rattachent
  • Connaissance des principes juridiques et du droit administratif, tels que l’équité procédurale, la confidentialité, la protection de la vie privée, les droits de la personne et le droit de la preuve
  • Capacité à acquérir des connaissances sur la Loi sur le Collège, les règlements, le Règlement administratif et le Code de déontologie
  • Connaissance de logiciels bureautiques et administratifs

Ce que nous offrons

Le processus d’embauche et d’accueil du Collège se fait entièrement à distance

  • L’occasion de protéger l’intérêt public relativement à l’immigration et la citoyenneté
  • Une culture de transparence où les membres de l’équipe participent aux conversations importantes
  • Prestations-maladie complètes dès le premier jour, pour vous et votre famille
  • Accès au programme d’aide aux employés et à leur famille

Pour postuler

Cliquez ici pour téléverser votre curriculum vitæ et une courte lettre de présentation indiquant les raisons pour lesquelles vous estimez être à même d’assumer ce rôle.

Vos renseignements personnels sont recueillis et utilisés par le Collège lorsque vous postulez pour un emploi auprès du Collège. Veuillez lire l’avis de confidentialité du Collège pour en savoir plus sur ses pratiques relatives à la protection de la vie privée.

Le Collège est un employeur qui souscrit au principe de l’égalité d’accès à l’emploi. Nous acceptons les candidatures des personnes légalement autorisées à travailler au Canada, qui représentent la diversité de notre pays, et dont les qualifications satisfont aux compétences et expériences que nous recherchons. Nous sommes résolus à offrir des chances égales à tous les candidats et à respecter les besoins des personnes ayant un handicap. Si nous communiquons avec vous au sujet d’une occasion d’emploi et que vous avez besoin d’une mesure d’adaptation en raison d’un handicap, nous nous ferons un plaisir de collaborer avec vous pour déterminer comment vous soutenir le mieux possible dans le cadre de ce processus.

Ciência de Dados tem como objetivo desbravar novos caminhos para permitir que as empresas respondam às suas questões mais urgentes. Além disso, trabalhamos em colaboração com acadêmicos de destaque, especialistas do setor e engenheiros altamente qualificados para capacitar nossos clientes a gerar insights sofisticados e inéditos a partir dos maiores volumes de big data.

Como Cientista de Dados, você será responsável por contribuir para a estratégia de negócios e influenciar a tomada de decisões por meio de insights obtidos a partir da análise de dados complexos. Você irá projetar e desenvolver soluções baseadas em inteligência artificial, incluindo aplicações de IA generativa, colaborando com líderes de negócio, engenheiros e especialistas do setor para transformar e modernizar tecnologias e processos da Dell.   • Projetar, desenvolver e avaliar modelos preditivos, algoritmos, motores probabilísticos e processos para consolidar, analisar e gerar insights a partir de dados complexos e não estruturados.
  • Desenvolver e executar testes para validar a eficácia de algoritmos em diferentes casos de uso analíticos, incluindo testes rigorosos, validação e avaliação de desempenho de soluções de IA.
  • Manter-se atualizado sobre os avanços em pesquisas de inteligência artificial e aplicar técnicas de ponta para aprimorar o desempenho dos modelos e gerar recomendações acionáveis para o negócio.

  • Sólido conhecimento dos conceitos de Data Science e Inteligência Artificial Generativa, incluindo experiência com grandes modelos de linguagem (LLMs) e familiaridade com técnicas e aplicações de Processamento de Linguagem Natural (NLP).
  • Fortes habilidades de programação em Python, experiência com ferramentas colaborativas de desenvolvimento, como GitLab e Jira, além de conhecimento em projeto e análise de algoritmos.
  • Base sólida em matemática e estatística, com capacidade para interpretar conjuntos de dados complexos e gerar insights acionáveis.

Requisitos Desejáveis

  • Sólido conhecimento e proficiência em sistemas agentic.
  • Mestrado ou Doutorado em Inteligência Artificial, Machine Learning, Data Science ou áreas relacionadas, concluído ou em andamento.

jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Insurance Finance

Corporate Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Risk Management

Regulatory Reporting

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

Strong in complex financial decision-making

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

Goldbelt Incorporated is an Alaska Native Corporation (ANC) headquartered in Juneau, Alaska, whose mission is to make a significant and positive difference in the lives of more than 4,200 Alaska Native shareholders. Alaska Native Corporations hold a distinct purpose and share a familiar creation story born in an act of Congress in 1971. Join a fast-growing “forever” company that manages over 30 subsidiaries and provides centers of excellence in a shared service center model based out of Herndon, Virginia. At Goldbelt, we place a strong emphasis on recognizing and rewarding the dedication and hard work of our team members in pursuit of our company's mission. We are a team focused on gold standard customer service and professional growth with competitive benefits and profit-sharing plans and help support a business model that gives back to the community of shareholders.

Summary:

The Cloud Administrator will be responsible for managing, monitoring, and optimizing Goldbelt's cloud-based infrastructure. This role requires deep expertise in cloud services, security, and automation, with an emphasis on maintaining high levels of system availability, performance, and security across multiple cloud platforms. As a Cloud Administrator, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless integration of cloud-based solutions into our business processes, maintain cost-effective solutions, and continuously improve our cloud infrastructure to support our growing needs.

This is a remote position, must be willing to support our core hours of 8am-5pm EST.

Qualifications

Necessary Skills and Knowledge:

  • Strong understanding of cloud security principles and best practices
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex issues
  • Ability to embrace change, learn quickly, and thrive in a dynamic corporate environment
  • Skill in working harmoniously within cross-functional teams to achieve common objectives
  • Ability to prioritize tasks, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines
  • Must have the ability to communicate effectively and diplomatically, both verbally and in writing, with co-workers and with outside agencies, partners, shareholders, and business associates
  • Strong cultural awareness and sensitivity, with the ability to adapt messages and strategies for diverse audiences
  • Strong understanding of relevant software, tools, and systems used in the corporate environment. This includes a proficiency in standard software applications, including Windows and MS Office Suite (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel)

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s of Science in Information Technology, or equivalent years of experience
  • Certified in AZ-500, MS-500, MS-700, AZ-104, or SC-400 or equivalent certification.
  • Minimum of five years in Information Technology
  • Proven experience in cloud administration, with expertise Azure and other SaaS applications
  • Ability to successfully pass a background check
  • Must be able to support core hours of 8am to 5pm EST (eastern standard time)
  • Must be willing to travel up to 25% of the time

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Six or more years of experience in support of Azure Cloud
  • Certified as an Azure Administrator Associate, MS-102 Administrator Expert, or equivalent certifications
  • Relevant certifications such as ITIL, CISM, or equivalent certifications
  • Experience and adherence to compliance frameworks: (CMMC Level 2, GovHigh, 32CFR, CUI, FedRAMP, NIST-800, PCI-DSS, HIPAA/HITECH, SOC 1 & SOC 2) and internal security best practices
  • Experience with automation tools and scripting languages
  • Local candidates and Shareholders of Goldbelt are strongly preferred
  • Experience working with 8(a) companies
  • Previous experience working with Alaska Native Corporations (ANCs)
  • Previous government contracting experience

Pay and Benefits

The salary range for this position is $112,700 to $137,750 annually.

At Goldbelt, we value and reward our team's dedication and hard work. We provide a competitive base salary commensurate with your qualifications and experience. Our annual incentive compensation plan is designed to reward your contributions to Goldbelt's success. It's a profit-sharing initiative tied to our strategic objectives, demonstrating that your efforts directly impact our achievements. As an employee, you'll also enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with company matching, tax-deferred savings options, supplementary benefits, paid time off, and professional development opportunities.

Responsibilities

Essential Job Functions:

  • Cloud Infrastructure Management: Configure, monitor, and maintain the company’s cloud environments (e.g., Azure, AWS, SaaS) to ensure optimal performance and scalability
  • Security and Compliance: Ensure infrastructure security and compliance by monitoring access, usage, and resources
  • System Backups and Recovery: Perform system backups and recovery to maintain data integrity and availability
  • Technical Support: Provide technical support for cloud applications and services, and train end users as needed
  • Collaboration: Work closely with IT security teams to monitor the company’s cloud privacy and respond to technical issues in a timely and efficient manner

UX/UI Designer (Product Design, Figma & User Experience)

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a UX/UI Designer to own the full product design lifecycle—from user research and wireframes to polished interfaces and developer-ready handoffs.

This is more than a visual design role. You’ll work closely with product managers, engineers, and stakeholders to create intuitive, scalable, and user-friendly web and mobile experiences that improve usability, engagement, and conversion.

Responsibilities

User Research & Product Design

  • Conduct user research, interviews, surveys, and usability testing.
  • Create personas, user journeys, and user flows.
  • Analyze user behavior using tools like Hotjar, FullStory, or Google Analytics.
  • Translate insights into product improvements.

Wireframing & Prototyping

  • Design wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, and interactive prototypes.
  • Build product flows using Figma, Adobe XD, or Sketch.
  • Iterate designs based on user feedback and stakeholder input.

UI Design & Design Systems

  • Design responsive, modern user interfaces for web and mobile products.
  • Build and maintain design systems, component libraries, and style guides.
  • Ensure visual consistency across all product experiences.

Collaboration & Developer Handoff

  • Work closely with product managers, engineers, and QA teams.
  • Deliver developer-ready designs, specifications, assets, and documentation.
  • Support handoffs using Figma Dev Mode, Zeplin, or similar tools.

Optimization & Accessibility

  • Improve onboarding flows, usability, and product engagement.
  • Design with WCAG accessibility standards and responsive best practices.
  • Participate in design reviews, usability testing, and A/B testing.

Required Experience & Skills

  • 2+ years of UX/UI or Product Design experience.
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating UX thinking and high-quality UI design.
  • Proficiency with Figma, Adobe XD, or Sketch.
  • Experience with wireframing, prototyping, responsive design, and design systems.
  • Strong understanding of user-centered design and accessibility principles.

Nice to Have

  • Experience designing SaaS, mobile, or e-commerce products.
  • Basic understanding of HTML/CSS.
  • Experience with analytics tools, user testing platforms, or enterprise design systems.

What Success Looks Like

  • Intuitive, user-friendly product experiences.
  • Clean, scalable, developer-ready designs.
  • Improved usability, engagement, and conversion.
  • Consistent design systems across products.
  • On-time delivery of high-quality design assets.

Interview Process

  • Initial Recruiter Screening
  • Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  • Portfolio Review & Practical Design Task
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Onboarding

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. It’s a short, self-recorded video that completes your application and allows hiring managers to get to know you before the interview process begins.

Rather than repeating your background during multiple screening calls, you’ll tell your story once, allowing future interviews to focus on meaningful conversations.

Don’t overthink it—you can record as many takes as you’d like before submitting. Your invitation will come from Spark Hire, so please check both your inbox and spam folder.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Resource Planning and Forecasting
jobs.excerpt: OverviewHealthEdge® offers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance companies, guaranteeing an enduring financial edge in an increasingly competitive market.
jobs.description:
Overview

HealthEdge® offers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance companies, guaranteeing an enduring financial edge in an increasingly competitive market. We're experiencing strong market momentum, with a growing number of health plans choosing HealthEdge to modernize their operations and compete more effectively. As we expand, we're investing in the people who power that growth, making this a pivotal moment to join us and shape the future of healthcare technology. Learn more at HealthEdge.com.

Role Summary

The Senior Manager, Resource Planning & Forecasting leads a centralized Resource Planning function serving both Contact Center and Back Office operations, establishing a single planning discipline across every workforce-intensive function. This role owns the accuracy and integrity of all volume, workload and staffing forecasts, builds and mentors the resource planning team, and is a trusted advisor to senior operational, Finance and HR leaders on workforce demand and staffing risk.

What You'll Own

Leadership & Strategy

  • Lead and develop a centralized Resource Planning function that serves both Contact Center and Back Office operations, establishing a consistent planning discipline across all workforce-intensive functions
  • Define the vision, standards and operating model for forecasting and capacity planning across the organization, ensuring methodologies are rigorous, repeatable and scalable
  • Build and mentor a team of resource planning analysts, fostering a culture of analytical excellence, continuous improvement and strong cross-functional partnership
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to senior operational, Finance and HR leaders on workforce demand, staffing risk and planning assumptions that inform business decisions

Forecasting & Planning Oversight

  • Own the accuracy and integrity of all volume, workload and staffing forecasts across Contact Center and Back Office functions, setting standards for model governance and variance accountability
  • Ensure forecasting models are maintained and continuously refined to reflect changes in business drivers, productivity assumptions, regulatory requirements and operational realities
  • Oversee the production of short-range and long-range staffing requirement outputs, ensuring planning horizons and lead times are sufficient to drive timely hiring and operational decisions
  • Drive alignment between Resource Planning outputs and downstream WFM scheduling teams, ensuring capacity plans translate effectively into executable staffing and work distribution models

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner closely with Finance during budget cycles to ensure headcount plans are grounded in validated demand forecasts and productivity assumptions
  • Collaborate with HR and Talent Acquisition to translate staffing requirement outputs into actionable hiring timelines, ensuring workforce gaps are addressed proactively
  • Engage regularly with Contact Center and Back Office operational leaders to align on planning assumptions, communicate capacity risks and build shared accountability for forecast accuracy
  • Work in close partnership with the WFM Scheduling and Real-Time Monitoring teams to ensure a seamless handoff between capacity planning outputs and day-to-day scheduling execution

Reporting, Insights & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish a consistent cadence of capacity outlook reporting for senior leadership, providing clear visibility into staffing risks, hiring needs and planning confidence levels across all functions
  • Champion the use of data and analytics to drive planning decisions, identifying opportunities to improve forecast accuracy, reduce variance and strengthen the organization's planning maturity
  • Lead post-mortem reviews of significant forecast variances, translating findings into model improvements and updated planning assumptions
  • Evaluate and implement workforce planning tools and technologies that enhance the team's forecasting capabilities and operational efficiency

Governance & Compliance

  • Ensure back-office capacity plans reflect applicable regulatory turnaround requirements (e.g., CMS timelines for Utilization Management determinations), embedding compliance considerations into planning models and staffing recommendations
  • Maintain documentation of planning methodologies, assumptions and model logic to support auditability, knowledge transfer and organizational consistency
  • Define and monitor key performance indicators for the Resource Planning function itself, including forecast accuracy, planning cycle timeliness and stakeholder satisfaction

Leadership Competencies

Integrity & Trust — the threshold expectation for every role at HealthEdge, above and ahead of the competency framework.

Core competencies for this role:

  • Lead & Inspire
  • Develop Self & Others

What You Bring

  • 7 or more years of progressive experience in workforce planning, forecasting or capacity planning, including experience spanning both contact center and back office / operations environments
  • 3 or more years of experience building and leading a team of analysts or planners
  • Demonstrated ability to build a planning discipline and operating model from the ground up, including standards, governance and model methodology
  • Strong track record partnering with Finance and HR on headcount planning, budget cycles and hiring timelines
  • Executive-level communication skills; comfort presenting capacity risk and planning confidence to senior leadership
  • Working knowledge of regulatory turnaround requirements relevant to health plan operations (e.g., CMS UM determination timelines)

What Success Looks Like

  • Contact Center and Back Office operate under one consistent, well-governed planning discipline with forecast accuracy tracked and improving over time
  • Senior leadership has reliable, recurring visibility into staffing risk, hiring needs and planning confidence across every workforce-intensive function
  • The Resource Planning team is a trusted, high-functioning partner to Finance, HR and operational leadership, and analysts are developing into stronger planners under the Director's mentorship

Geographic Responsibility: Remote, US

Type of Employment: Full-time, permanent

FLSA Classification (USA Only): Exempt

Work Environment: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job: 

  • The employee is occasionally required to move around the office. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Work across multiple time zones in a hybrid or remote work environment.
  • Long periods of time sitting and/or standing in front of a computer using video technology.
  • May require travel dependent on company needs.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of the job being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. HealthEdge reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary. In addition, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Candidates may be required to go through a pre-employment criminal background check.

HealthEdge is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to workforce diversity and actively encourage all qualified persons to seek employment with us, including, but not limited to, racial and ethnic minorities, women, veterans and persons with disabilities.

**The annual US base salary range for this position is $165,000 to $179,000. This salary range may cover multiple career levels at HealthEdge. Final compensation will be determined during the interview process and is based on a combination of factors including, but not limited to, your skills, experience, qualifications and education.
